parameters.risk_free_treatment: RF IS NOT SUBTRACTED FROM ANYTHING. All five series are already excess or long-short returns by construction: Mkt-RF is the value-weight market return minus the one-month Treasury bill rate, and SMB, HML, RMW and CMA are zero-net-investment long-short spreads whose financing is already netted inside the spread. Subtracting RF from a long-short spread is the classic error in this exercise and it is invisible in the output, because the result is still a plausible-looking small monthly number. The Sharpe ratios below are therefore mean / standard deviation of the series as distributed, with a risk-free rate of exactly zero, and the code asserts that zero rather than defaulting to it. Within the frozen window the RF column is in any case the Ibbotson Associates series, the same source the authors used; the file's own preamble records that RF switches to ICE BofA only from 202406, which is outside this window and therefore cannot affect this reproduction.

source_pin.vintage_caveat: The sha256 pins WHICH FILE was used. It does not and cannot establish that the file represents what was publicly available in 2014. Ken French publishes no vintage archive, so the 2013-2014 CRSP vintage the paper used is not obtainable and an exactly like-for-like reproduction is not available to this repository at any tolerance.

gate.justification: Declared before any number was computed. The mean tolerance of 0.02 percentage points per month is 0.24 percentage points per year, which is about 4% of the printed market premium and about 6% of the printed HML premium; a restatement larger than that would materially move any downstream premium estimate, which is where a gate protecting downstream work belongs. The standard-deviation tolerance of 0.05 percentage points per month is roughly 1% relative on the market factor and 2.5% on CMA. The t-statistic tolerance is DERIVED, not independent: with T = 606, t = mean * sqrt(606) / sd, so a 0.02 move in the mean of the smallest-standard-deviation factor (CMA, printed 2.01) moves t by 0.02 * 24.62 / 2.01 = 0.245. Rounding it up to 0.30 keeps the t tolerance implied by the mean and standard-deviation tolerances rather than binding ahead of them, so the gate is decided by the two primitive statistics.

implementation_error.purpose: Five times the gate. A difference this large in a 606-month average, or a sign flip, is not a data revision; it is a bug. It fires the falsifier rather than producing `unresolved`.

print_exact_diagnostic.purpose: Diagnostic only; never gating. A cell inside this band rounds to the printed value, so the currently distributed data are numerically indistinguishable from the published vintage at printing precision for that cell. A cell outside it but inside the gate is evidence of a real but immaterial revision. Separating these two is the whole reason the difference is measured rather than merely tested.

units.note: The percent-to-decimal-to-percent round trip is deliberate and is the point of running the comparison through the real parser rather than reading the CSV again. A factor of 100 in either direction is the single most likely silent error in this path and it is the one the printed table catches.

cost_illustration.k_source: Novy-Marx and Velikov (2016), value-weighted decile long-short, 1963-2012. k runs 1.57-1.71 across their three turnover tiers; 1.0 is the conservative floor for patient execution in liquid names.

UMD.basis: monthly rebalance on 2-12 month prior return

cost_illustration.published_outcome_to_keep_in_view: Novy-Marx and Velikov find a 17% haircut in the low-turnover tier and 144% in the high-turnover tier, where four of six strategies had strictly negative net returns. The ordering of factors by gross premium is therefore not the ordering by net premium, and this experiment cannot establish the latter.
cost_illustration.purpose: NOT a haircut and NOT a net return. The cost model is reported as a SEPARATE column showing the order of magnitude of the implementation gap for a tradable strategy of comparable turnover, so that the gross premia below cannot be read as achievable. The French series themselves have no turnover, no holdings and no tradable form, so no net figure for them exists to be computed.
cost_illustration.turnover_source: The published tier ranges are low 1.2-7.2%, mid 14-35%, high 90-94% one-sided per month. UMD's optimistic figure is the mid-tier implied mean of 27.5% and its pessimistic figure the high-tier implied mean of 91.5%, because French's six-portfolio 30/70 momentum construction turns over less than a decile long-short but is unambiguously in the high-turnover family. These are ASSUMPTIONS declared before the run, not measurements: turnover cannot be recovered from a return series.

parameters.missing_data_policy: A month missing from any required series drops that month from every factor in the same statistic, and the count of dropped months is reported. Series are never forward-filled.

also_report: realised power to detect the materiality threshold of 2.0 percentage points per year in that cell
realised power to detect 0.55% per month gross, Harvey, Liu and Zhu's (2016) structural estimate of the mean return of a genuinely true factor, which is 6.6 percentage points per year
the same MDE recomputed from the HAC standard error rather than sigma / sqrt(T), because monthly factor returns are autocorrelated and the closed form understates the required effect when they are
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true annualised premium that a test of the given size would reject the null for with probability power_target, given the era's realised volatility and length: MDE_monthly = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sigma / sqrt(T), annualised by 12.
power.purpose: So that a cell failing to exclude zero can be read as "this window cannot tell" rather than "there is no premium". This is the single most important statistical output of the experiment and it is required for every cell, including the cells that do reject.

primary_grid.dependence_warning: These 20 tests are strongly dependent. The five eras of a factor nest; RMW and CMA share every era; all four factors are long-short spreads built from overlapping holdings of the same universe. A Benjamini-Hochberg correction that treats them as independent is therefore a LOWER BOUND on the true correction, and is reported as such.
primary_grid.description: The predeclared multiple-testing family: 4 factors x 5 era roles = 20 cells. Alternative-date eras (hml_post_rosenberg_alternative, umd_post_carhart_alternative) and hostile-test variants are OUTSIDE this family and are never counted as discoveries. Fixing the family before the run is what stops the correction from being applied to whichever subset survives.

CMA.alternative_date_tested: 2016-01, the era named `recent`. The 2009-01 asset-growth date is NOT tested as an era, because it would place the "post-publication" window inside the authors' own estimation sample, which would confound decay with in-sample fit rather than measure it. This is recorded as a known limitation rather than papered over.
CMA.defining_publication: Fama and French (2015), as for RMW.
predecessor_evidence:
Titman, Wei and Xie (2004), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 39(4), 677-700 - capital investment and the cross-section.
Cooper, Gulen and Schill (2008), Journal of Finance 63(4), 1609-1651 - asset growth, seven years before CMA. Its first January after publication is 2009-01, so CMA's effective discovery date is the most disputed of the four and 2014-01 is the most generous of the candidates.

HML.alternative_date_tested: 1986-01, the first January after Rosenberg, Reid and Lanstein (1985), as era hml_post_rosenberg_alternative.
HML.boundary_justification: The first January strictly after the February 1993 issue. 1993-01 to 1993-12 is dropped rather than assigned to either side, because the result was in print for ten of those twelve months.
HML.defining_publication: Fama and French (1993), "Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds", Journal of Financial Economics 33(1), 3-56, February 1993 issue. This is where HML is defined as a factor.
predecessor_evidence:
Basu (1977), Journal of Finance 32(3), 663-682 - price-earnings sorts.
Rosenberg, Reid and Lanstein (1985), Journal of Portfolio Management 11(3), 9-16 - book-to-market directly, eight years earlier.
De Bondt and Thaler (1985), Journal of Finance 40(3), 793-805 - long-horizon overreaction, a competing explanation of the same spread.
Fama and French (1992), Journal of Finance 47(2), 427-465, June 1992 - the cross-sectional result one year before the factor definition.

RMW.alternative_date_tested: 2016-01, the first January after the April 2015 journal issue, which is the era named `recent`.
RMW.boundary_justification: 2014-01 is the first month outside the authors' own estimation sample and follows the 2013 circulation of the working paper, so it is genuinely out-of-sample with respect to the discovery. It PRECEDES the April 2015 journal issue, which is why the alternative below is also reported.
RMW.defining_publication: Fama and French (2015), "A five-factor asset pricing model", Journal of Financial Economics 116(1), 1-22, April 2015 issue, whose sample ends 2013-12. The working paper circulated from 2013.
predecessor_evidence: Novy-Marx (2013), Journal of Financial Economics 108(1), 1-28, April 2013 - gross profitability, two years before RMW. Its own first January after publication is 2014-01, which coincides with the primary boundary; the two candidate discovery dates therefore agree for RMW.

UMD.alternative_date_tested: 1998-01, the first January after Carhart (1997), as era umd_post_carhart_alternative.
UMD.boundary_justification: The first January strictly after the March 1993 issue.
UMD.construction_caveat: The window 1965-01 to 1989-12 is Jegadeesh and Titman's main sample. The series is French's six-portfolio 30/70 UMD, which is a different construction from their decile 6-6 strategies. The window is theirs; the data are not.
UMD.defining_publication: Jegadeesh and Titman (1993), "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers", Journal of Finance 48(1), 65-91, March 1993 issue.
predecessor_evidence: Carhart (1997), Journal of Finance 52(1), 57-82, March 1997, is not a predecessor but a successor; it is when momentum entered the standard factor model, which is arguably when it became widely traded.
UMD.sample_caveat: 1965-1989 is their MAIN sample, not their only one: their Section VII additionally back-tests 1927-1964. French's UMD series also starts in 1927. There is therefore no window of the momentum series that is genuinely unseen by the discovering authors, which is a limitation of the original-sample era for UMD specifically and is not repairable from this data.

publication_record.policy: Every era boundary below is justified from the publication record, not chosen as a round number. A boundary is set at the first January that strictly follows the journal issue date, so that no month of a "post-publication" era can precede the printed result. Predecessor evidence is recorded because it means none of these dates is a clean discovery date.
publication_record.verification: Every journal, volume, issue, page range and ISSUE MONTH below was checked against publisher-deposited Crossref metadata for the article's DOI, and the sample periods against the article full text, on 2026-08-11. All eleven citations verified with no correction to any field used to set a boundary. The Fama and French (2015) working paper's own title page reads "First draft: June 2013 / This draft: November 2013", which is the primary evidence for the 2013 circulation date.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: Long-short factor returns are already excess returns by construction. RF is NOT subtracted a second time. This is recorded because subtracting it twice is a plausible and invisible error.

second_moment_uncertainty.application_rule: volatility in [sigma * (1 - u), sigma * (1 + u)] and therefore Sharpe in [S / (1 + u), S / (1 - u)], applied symmetrically because the direction of the error is unknown: the printed vintage is not established to be more correct than the current one, only different.
second_moment_uncertainty.consequence: This is a SYSTEMATIC uncertainty in the denominator, not sampling error. It does not shrink with more data and it is not in any bootstrap interval. Any statistic in this experiment that divides by an HML or RMW volatility - the Sharpe ratio above all, and the minimum detectable effect, which is proportional to volatility - must carry this band ALONGSIDE its sampling interval, reported separately and never combined into one number. Where a conclusion would flip inside the band, the output must say so explicitly. Means, and therefore the primary metric, are unaffected.
second_moment_uncertainty.finding: The Phase 1 ingestion gate came back UNRESOLVED, not PASS. All five monthly means, all five t-statistics and all ten cross-factor correlations reproduce Fama and French (2015) Table 4 within the predeclared tolerance. The standard deviations of HML and RMW do not, against two independently typeset vintages: variance ratios of 0.940 and 1.104, i.e. this repository's HML standard deviation is 3.03% below the printed 2.88 and its RMW standard deviation is 5.09% above the printed 2.14.

relative_band_on_volatility.note: CMA reproduced to 0.53% and the market factor to 0.14%, both inside the gate, so no band is carried for them. UMD is from a different file that was never gated against a printed table, so its band is unmeasured rather than zero, and that is stated in the output instead of a number.

source_pin.policy: Both files are pinned by the sha256 of their raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current CRSP vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download, and a premium computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. The normalized hash additionally catches a parser change that leaves the downloaded bytes identical.

series.column_rename: The file calls the series `Mom`. This experiment calls it UMD throughout. The rename is recorded here rather than assumed in code.

publication_record.verification: Every journal, volume, issue, page range and ISSUE MONTH below was checked against publisher-deposited Crossref metadata for the article's DOI, and the sample periods against the article full text, on 2026-08-11. All eleven citations verified with no correction to any field used to set a boundary. The Fama and French (2015) working paper's own title page reads "First draft: June 2013 / This draft: November 2013", which is the primary evidence for the 2013 circulation date.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: Long-short factor returns are already excess returns by construction. RF is NOT subtracted a second time. This is recorded because subtracting it twice is a plausible and invisible error.

second_moment_uncertainty.application_rule: volatility in [sigma * (1 - u), sigma * (1 + u)] and therefore Sharpe in [S / (1 + u), S / (1 - u)], applied symmetrically because the direction of the error is unknown: the printed vintage is not established to be more correct than the current one, only different.
second_moment_uncertainty.consequence: This is a SYSTEMATIC uncertainty in the denominator, not sampling error. It does not shrink with more data and it is not in any bootstrap interval. Any statistic in this experiment that divides by an HML or RMW volatility - the Sharpe ratio above all, and the minimum detectable effect, which is proportional to volatility - must carry this band ALONGSIDE its sampling interval, reported separately and never combined into one number. Where a conclusion would flip inside the band, the output must say so explicitly. Means, and therefore the primary metric, are unaffected.
second_moment_uncertainty.finding: The Phase 1 ingestion gate came back UNRESOLVED, not PASS. All five monthly means, all five t-statistics and all ten cross-factor correlations reproduce Fama and French (2015) Table 4 within the predeclared tolerance. The standard deviations of HML and RMW do not, against two independently typeset vintages: variance ratios of 0.940 and 1.104, i.e. this repository's HML standard deviation is 3.03% below the printed 2.88 and its RMW standard deviation is 5.09% above the printed 2.14.

relative_band_on_volatility.note: CMA reproduced to 0.53% and the market factor to 0.14%, both inside the gate, so no band is carried for them. UMD is from a different file that was never gated against a printed table, so its band is unmeasured rather than zero, and that is stated in the output instead of a number.

source_pin.policy: Both files are pinned by the sha256 of their raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current CRSP vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download, and a premium computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. The normalized hash additionally catches a parser change that leaves the downloaded bytes identical.

series.column_rename: The file calls the series `Mom`. This experiment calls it UMD throughout. The rename is recorded here rather than assumed in code.

attribution.rationale: Goyal and Jegadeesh (2018) show the strategy carries a large embedded net-long market position and that adding a time-varying market position to a cross-sectional strategy reproduces the time-series result. The decisive test is therefore whether a static market exposure plus a volatility-scaled market position reproduces the sleeve. The absolute market term is a convexity proxy: a strategy that is genuinely long crisis convexity should load positively on it. The lagged market term captures the slow signal.
attribution.replica_caveat: The replica is fitted on the same sample it is evaluated on, so its marginal benefit is an UPPER bound. That is the conservative direction for this test: it makes clause (d) of the falsifier easier to fire, which is correct, because the question is whether a simpler exposure COULD explain the result.

bond_proxy.construction: A ten-year Treasury total return reconstructed from FRED GS10 by the standard duration-and-convexity approximation on a par bond: r_t = y_{t-1}/12 - D_t (y_t - y_{t-1}) + 0.5 C_t (y_t - y_{t-1})^2, with D_t and C_t the modified duration and convexity of a ten-year par bond at y_{t-1}.
bond_proxy.used_as: declared robustness arm only, never the primary benchmark
bond_proxy.warning: This is a MODELLED series, not an investable total-return history. It has no documented total-return contract, no coupon reinvestment convention and no transaction costs. It exists so that the 2022 window, in which equities and bonds fell together, is not silently removed from the experiment by the absence of a bond leg. No conclusion may rest on it alone.

parameters.cash_series_rationale: TB3MS is the monthly average secondary-market three-month Treasury bill rate on a discount basis: the conventional monthly cash proxy in the US asset-pricing literature, at the same monthly frequency as every other series here, and the series against which the vendor's "excess return" is most nearly defined. DGS3MO and DFF are registered in this repository and were NOT used: DGS3MO is a daily constant-maturity interpolated yield on a different basis and DFF is an overnight interbank rate with no three-month maturity. Swapping them moves a Sharpe ratio, so the choice is declared here and not revisited after seeing a result.

evaluation_disclosure.author_interest: The series is maintained by a firm that sells the strategy. This is not an accusation; it is a recorded conflict that raises the required evidential standard.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: This experiment evaluates a published, author-maintained vendor series. It is NOT an independent replication of time-series momentum. An independent reimplementation would require contract-level futures histories, roll conventions, collateral returns, execution assumptions and point-in-time market availability, none of which are inputs here. Any write-up that describes this as a replication is wrong, and the archived workbook, sheet, and revision date must accompany every figure because vendor URLs, workbooks and revisions change.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS the experiment. AQR reconstructs its full history on every update and Ken French rebuilds his from each new CRSP vintage, so an unrecognised hash is a new vintage rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. FRED hashes change whenever a new observation is appended, so the FRED pins are recorded and reported but do NOT abort; the abort applies to the two sources whose history is rewritten in place.

volatility_estimator.form: Exponentially weighted variance of lagged returns with the centre of mass stated in the vendor's own recovered methodology text: sigma_t^2 = k * sum_i (1-delta) delta^i (r_{t-1-i} - rbar_t)^2 with delta / (1 - delta) = the centre of mass, and k the annualisation factor.
volatility_estimator.this_repository_form: The public series is MONTHLY, so a daily estimator is not computable from it. The identical exponentially weighted form is applied to monthly returns at the same calendar centre of mass, days / 21, with k = 12. The 60-, 20- and 120-day lookbacks become 2.857, 0.952 and 5.714 months. This is an approximation of the vendor's estimator, not the vendor's estimator, and the frozen day-based values are retained above so that the translation stays visible.
volatility_estimator.vendor_form: The vendor applies this to DAILY returns with a 60-day centre of mass and k = 261, and uses the estimate at t-1 on the returns at t. Both facts come from text recovered from the workbook's embedded picture, not from cells.

parameters.volatility_target_policy: The volatility-scaled passive comparator targets the passive benchmark's own realised volatility computed on an EXPANDING window ending at t-1. A full-sample target would be a look-ahead normalisation, and a fixed number would be a tuned parameter.

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) would understate the standard error by a factor of 3.46 and shrink far too little.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. Taking true gross alpha as normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation sigma_true = 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010), against a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed_alpha with shrinkage_factor = sigma_true^2 / (sigma_true^2 + SE^2).
alpha_shrinkage.worked_example: At the reference standard error the factor is 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + 3.36^2) = 0.121, so an observed 5%/yr alpha implies a posterior near 0.6%/yr. The factor is recomputed from each fund's OWN HAC standard error rather than reused, because a fund with a tighter standard error is shrunk less and hardcoding 0.121 would be wrong for every fund.

parameters.cash_series_alternatives_rationale: All three are substituted in a hostile test and the effect on every excess return is reported, so that the choice above is shown not to have made the answer. They are NOT interchangeable with each other or with the one-month bill: different maturities, frequencies and constructions.
parameters.cash_series_rationale: The one-month Treasury bill rate distributed in the SAME French file as the factors, used to build every excess return in this experiment. The reason is not convenience: Mkt-RF is defined as the market return LESS THIS RATE, so a regression intercept is only interpretable as alpha when the dependent variable's excess return is taken over the same rate. Using a different cash series would push the difference between the two rates straight into every alpha. It is frozen here so it cannot be swapped for whichever series improves a result.

concretisation_log.change: Return source fixed as SEC Form N-PORT Item B.5, with the Yahoo chart endpoint demoted to an independent cross-check.
concretisation_log.reason: The original specification required "a source with documented total-return and corporate-action treatment" without naming one, and decision 0002 found no free PRICE feed qualifies. Form N-PORT is a regulatory disclosure rather than a price feed and carries a defined statistic, a permanent archive and a visible amendment trail.

concretisation_log.change: Sample policy moved from 2017-01..2025-12 with a 108-month minimum to 2020-01..2025-12 with a 72-month minimum.
concretisation_log.reason: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019Q4. 2020-01 is the first calendar month covered by every screened fund's filings whatever its fiscal quarter alignment, and it splits into two whole three-year halves. This is a data-availability constraint, not a choice about which window looked better; no return had been read when it was made.

concretisation_log.change: Minimum net assets raised from 100 million to 1,000 million USD at the frame date.
concretisation_log.reason: At 100 million the mechanical screen returned more than a hundred products, which would make the audit shallow and the multiple-testing family unwieldy. The threshold was chosen from the COUNT of funds at each level, which was visible before any return was downloaded, and never from performance.

concretisation_log.change: The exclusion pattern was extended to match the abbreviation "Intl" alongside "International".
concretisation_log.reason: The criterion was always "no non-US mandate"; one fund named "iShares Edge MSCI Multifactor Intl ETF" escaped the pattern on spelling alone. Fixing the pattern enforces the criterion that was already written rather than changing it.

concretisation_log.change: The frame was fixed as the 2019Q4 N-PORT census rather than a current fund list, and the 2025Q4 census was added purely to measure attrition.
concretisation_log.reason: A universe assembled from currently listed funds is survivorship contaminated by construction. Screening the census at the START of the window and following each fund forward makes the attrition a measurement instead of an omission.

concretisation_log.change: The intended-factor map, including the negative sign for growth mandates, was written into the specification.
concretisation_log.reason: Without it a fund could be graded against whichever loading turned out largest, which is the exposure-audit equivalent of choosing the benchmark after the result.

concretisation_log.change: The cash rate was changed from TB3MS to the one-month bill distributed in the same French file as the factors. TB3MS, DGS3MO and DFF were moved to the hostile tests.
concretisation_log.reason: Mkt-RF is the market return less the one-month bill. Taking the fund's excess return over a THREE-month bill instead would push the spread between the two maturities into every regression intercept and contaminate exactly the quantity the experiment is most careful about. The change makes the estimate correct rather than convenient, and every alternative is still reported.

concretisation_log.change: Realised taxable distributions and portfolio turnover were reclassified from reported metrics to recorded gaps.
concretisation_log.reason: Neither is in Form N-PORT. Both are in the annual report on Form N-CSR as unstructured HTML. Estimating them would be manufacturing a number the source does not contain, so they are recorded as missing instead.

concretisation_log.change: The alpha-shrinkage factor is recomputed from each fund's own standard error instead of using the framework's reference 0.121.
concretisation_log.reason: 0.121 is the factor at the reference standard error of 3.36%/yr. A fund whose own standard error differs must be shrunk by its own factor, and reusing the reference would be wrong for every fund in both directions.

primary.what: The fund's own monthly total return for each month of the reporting period, filed on Form NPORT-P per share class, in percent.
primary.why_it_is_still_exploratory: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, the figures are fund-reported and unaudited, and a frame taken in 2019Q4 cannot see a fund that died before it. Decision 0002 is NOT overturned: this remains exploratory and may not promote a sleeve.
primary.why_this_and_not_a_price_feed: Decision 0002 found that no free PRICE feed documents a total-return contract, a corporate-action policy, delisting coverage or a revision history. Form N-PORT is not a price feed. It is a signed regulatory disclosure of a defined statistic, permanently archived by the SEC, in which a correction is a separate document and the original stays readable. That is a materially stronger contract than any price feed tested, and it is why this experiment can be run at all.

secondary.status: EXPLORATORY and not research-grade, per decision 0002. Adjusted closes are recomputed on every request and no methodology is published.
secondary.used_for: An independent cross-check of the primary source over the same months, and nothing else. No result is estimated on it alone.
secondary.why: Two independent measurements of the same quantity make a silent adjustment error visible. Agreement is evidence about the data, not about the strategy.

tax_rates.note: Used ONLY to convert observed distributions into a net-pessimistic cost column for a stated hypothetical account. This is not an after-tax experiment: there are no tax lots, holding periods, harvesting rules or account modelling here, and no constant haircut is applied to returns.

validation_gates.cross_source_gate: Where both sources have a month, the median absolute difference between the N-PORT and Yahoo monthly returns is reported per fund. A large disagreement is a finding about the data and is reported rather than reconciled.
validation_gates.market_beta_gate: The broad-market comparator's regression on Mkt-RF must produce a beta within 0.05 of 1.00 and an R-squared of at least 0.98. A cheap total-market fund that does not reproduce the market factor means the data path is wrong, not that the fund is interesting.
validation_gates.month_alignment: Item B.5 reports rtn1 as the FIRST month of the reporting period and rtn3 as the month ending on repPdDate. A reversed reading would shift every history by two months and destroy every regression while leaving the numbers looking plausible. The alignment is therefore CHECKED, not assumed: the broad-market comparator's reconstructed series must correlate at least 0.99 with the French market factor and must show its largest single-month loss in 2020-03.

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) would understate the standard error by a factor of 3.46 and shrink far too little.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. Taking true gross alpha as normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation sigma_true = 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010), against a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed_alpha with shrinkage_factor = sigma_true^2 / (sigma_true^2 + SE^2).
alpha_shrinkage.worked_example: At the reference standard error the factor is 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + 3.36^2) = 0.121, so an observed 5%/yr alpha implies a posterior near 0.6%/yr. The factor is recomputed from each fund's OWN HAC standard error rather than reused, because a fund with a tighter standard error is shrunk less and hardcoding 0.121 would be wrong for every fund.

parameters.cash_series_alternatives_rationale: All three are substituted in a hostile test and the effect on every excess return is reported, so that the choice above is shown not to have made the answer. They are NOT interchangeable with each other or with the one-month bill: different maturities, frequencies and constructions.
parameters.cash_series_rationale: The one-month Treasury bill rate distributed in the SAME French file as the factors, used to build every excess return in this experiment. The reason is not convenience: Mkt-RF is defined as the market return LESS THIS RATE, so a regression intercept is only interpretable as alpha when the dependent variable's excess return is taken over the same rate. Using a different cash series would push the difference between the two rates straight into every alpha. It is frozen here so it cannot be swapped for whichever series improves a result.

concretisation_log.change: Return source fixed as SEC Form N-PORT Item B.5, with the Yahoo chart endpoint demoted to an independent cross-check.
concretisation_log.reason: The original specification required "a source with documented total-return and corporate-action treatment" without naming one, and decision 0002 found no free PRICE feed qualifies. Form N-PORT is a regulatory disclosure rather than a price feed and carries a defined statistic, a permanent archive and a visible amendment trail.

concretisation_log.change: Sample policy moved from 2017-01..2025-12 with a 108-month minimum to 2020-01..2025-12 with a 72-month minimum.
concretisation_log.reason: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019Q4. 2020-01 is the first calendar month covered by every screened fund's filings whatever its fiscal quarter alignment, and it splits into two whole three-year halves. This is a data-availability constraint, not a choice about which window looked better; no return had been read when it was made.

concretisation_log.change: Minimum net assets raised from 100 million to 1,000 million USD at the frame date.
concretisation_log.reason: At 100 million the mechanical screen returned more than a hundred products, which would make the audit shallow and the multiple-testing family unwieldy. The threshold was chosen from the COUNT of funds at each level, which was visible before any return was downloaded, and never from performance.

concretisation_log.change: The exclusion pattern was extended to match the abbreviation "Intl" alongside "International".
concretisation_log.reason: The criterion was always "no non-US mandate"; one fund named "iShares Edge MSCI Multifactor Intl ETF" escaped the pattern on spelling alone. Fixing the pattern enforces the criterion that was already written rather than changing it.

concretisation_log.change: The frame was fixed as the 2019Q4 N-PORT census rather than a current fund list, and the 2025Q4 census was added purely to measure attrition.
concretisation_log.reason: A universe assembled from currently listed funds is survivorship contaminated by construction. Screening the census at the START of the window and following each fund forward makes the attrition a measurement instead of an omission.

concretisation_log.change: The intended-factor map, including the negative sign for growth mandates, was written into the specification.
concretisation_log.reason: Without it a fund could be graded against whichever loading turned out largest, which is the exposure-audit equivalent of choosing the benchmark after the result.

concretisation_log.change: The cash rate was changed from TB3MS to the one-month bill distributed in the same French file as the factors. TB3MS, DGS3MO and DFF were moved to the hostile tests.
concretisation_log.reason: Mkt-RF is the market return less the one-month bill. Taking the fund's excess return over a THREE-month bill instead would push the spread between the two maturities into every regression intercept and contaminate exactly the quantity the experiment is most careful about. The change makes the estimate correct rather than convenient, and every alternative is still reported.

concretisation_log.change: Realised taxable distributions and portfolio turnover were reclassified from reported metrics to recorded gaps.
concretisation_log.reason: Neither is in Form N-PORT. Both are in the annual report on Form N-CSR as unstructured HTML. Estimating them would be manufacturing a number the source does not contain, so they are recorded as missing instead.

concretisation_log.change: The alpha-shrinkage factor is recomputed from each fund's own standard error instead of using the framework's reference 0.121.
concretisation_log.reason: 0.121 is the factor at the reference standard error of 3.36%/yr. A fund whose own standard error differs must be shrunk by its own factor, and reusing the reference would be wrong for every fund in both directions.

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) would understate the standard error by a factor of 3.46 and shrink far too little.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. Taking true gross alpha as normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation sigma_true = 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010), against a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed_alpha with shrinkage_factor = sigma_true^2 / (sigma_true^2 + SE^2).
alpha_shrinkage.worked_example: At the reference standard error the factor is 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + 3.36^2) = 0.121, so an observed 5%/yr alpha implies a posterior near 0.6%/yr. The factor is recomputed from each fund's OWN HAC standard error rather than reused, because a fund with a tighter standard error is shrunk less and hardcoding 0.121 would be wrong for every fund.

parameters.cash_series_alternatives_rationale: All three are substituted in a hostile test and the effect on every excess return is reported, so that the choice above is shown not to have made the answer. They are NOT interchangeable with each other or with the one-month bill: different maturities, frequencies and constructions.
parameters.cash_series_rationale: The one-month Treasury bill rate distributed in the SAME French file as the factors, used to build every excess return in this experiment. The reason is not convenience: Mkt-RF is defined as the market return LESS THIS RATE, so a regression intercept is only interpretable as alpha when the dependent variable's excess return is taken over the same rate. Using a different cash series would push the difference between the two rates straight into every alpha. It is frozen here so it cannot be swapped for whichever series improves a result.

notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_002_fund_exposure

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) would understate the standard error by a factor of 3.46 and shrink far too little.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. Taking true gross alpha as normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation sigma_true = 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010), against a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed_alpha with shrinkage_factor = sigma_true^2 / (sigma_true^2 + SE^2).
alpha_shrinkage.worked_example: At the reference standard error the factor is 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + 3.36^2) = 0.121, so an observed 5%/yr alpha implies a posterior near 0.6%/yr. The factor is recomputed from each fund's OWN HAC standard error rather than reused, because a fund with a tighter standard error is shrunk less and hardcoding 0.121 would be wrong for every fund.

parameters.cash_series_alternatives_rationale: All three are substituted in a hostile test and the effect on every excess return is reported, so that the choice above is shown not to have made the answer. parameters.cash_series_rationale: The one-month Treasury bill rate distributed in the SAME French file as the factors, used to build every excess return in this experiment. notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_002_fund_exposure

annualisation.mean: multiply the monthly arithmetic mean by 12
annualisation.note: sqrt(12) assumes serial independence, which monthly factor returns violate. The HAC standard error is reported precisely because that assumption is wrong, and the two are always shown side by side.
annualisation.volatility: multiply the monthly standard deviation by sqrt(12)

cross_region_bootstrap.method: Draw one set of stationary-bootstrap time indices of shape (n_resamples, months) with the frozen mean block length, and apply THE SAME row of indices to all three regional series at once. Because the composite is a fixed linear combination of contemporaneous regional observations, resampling the composite series with those indices is algebraically identical to resampling the panel and then compositing, and the implementation uses that identity.
cross_region_bootstrap.the_error_it_avoids: Resampling each region with its own independent index draw. That destroys the contemporaneous correlation, makes the composite behave like an average of three independent samples, and narrows the interval by a factor that grows with the true correlation. The independent version IS computed and reported beside the joint one, labelled invalid, because the size of the gap is itself a finding about how much a naive pooling would have overstated.
cross_region_bootstrap.what_it_preserves: Contemporaneous cross-region dependence, and short-range serial dependence within each region.

definitions_all_reported.reading: The number of independent regions the three actually amount to. Equals 3 under zero correlation and equal variances, and 1 under perfect correlation. Computed from the realised sample covariance over the era, not assumed.
The pooled evidence expressed in independent single-region months, ignoring serial dependence. Directly comparable to the observation count of an Experiment 001 cell.
The same quantity with serial dependence in the composite folded in. This is the honest measure and is expected to be the smallest of the three.
What treating the three regions as independent samples would claim. The ratio of this to the effective figures is the size of the error this experiment exists to avoid, and it is reported explicitly.

effective_sample_size.mde_definition: MDE_80 = 12 * (z_0.95 + z_0.80) * standard_error_of_the_monthly_mean, identical to exp_001. It is reported from the conventional standard error sigma/sqrt(T) of the composite AND from the composite's HAC standard error.
effective_sample_size.which_one_the_falsifier_reads: Branch (b) reads the CONVENTIONAL pooled MDE_80, which is the more generous of the two because it ignores autocorrelation. Firing branch (b) on the generous reading is a fortiori, and the HAC figure is reported beside it so that a reader can see how much more generous it was.
effective_sample_size.why: This is the decisive measurement of the experiment. Three regions of T months each supply 3T independent region-months only if the regions are uncorrelated. They are not, and how far short they fall is the number that decides branch (b).

episode_concentration.consequence: Clause a5 of the falsifier reads this. A pooled premium that does not survive dropping its own best calendar year cannot advance.
reported: the calendar-year contribution to every regional and pooled premium
the best calendar year of every regional and pooled cell, and the premium after it is dropped
whether the best calendar year is the SAME year across regions, which is the direct test of whether the regions share an episode
the two episodes exp_001 named, 2000 for HML and 2021 for RMW, evaluated in every region by name rather than by whichever year turned out best
episode_concentration.why: Experiment 001 found 79% of HML's entire US post-publication premium in the single year 2000 and 59% of RMW's in 2021. A premium that lives in one calendar year is a description of that year. Three regions that share the same episode are not three independent looks, and this experiment must say so rather than count them as three.

inherited_from_exp_001.era_inheritance: Every era in sample_policy is copied VERBATIM from exp_001_factor_decay.yaml, name and both boundaries unchanged. Experiment 005 exists to add regions, not to move a boundary, and moving one would make the two experiments incomparable while creating an unrecorded degree of freedom. The publication record that justifies each boundary is in exp_001_factor_decay.yaml under parameters.publication_record and is inherited unchanged rather than restated here, so that it has exactly one canonical home.
inherited: every era name and both of its boundaries, unchanged
the publication record and boundary justifications, by reference
the 2.0 percentage-point-per-year materiality threshold
the 80% power target and the closed-form minimum detectable effect
the frozen 12-month mean block length and its 6 and 24 month neighbours
the 10000 resample count and the 0.10 Benjamini-Hochberg alpha
the Phase 1 second-moment band on US HML and US RMW
the sample end of 2025-12 and the holdout beyond it
not_inherited: the original-sample eras, which precede both regional files
UMD, for which no regional file is manifested in this repository
the illustrative cost column, whose turnover assumptions are US-specific
inherited_from_exp_001.rule: Nothing inherited may be re-derived differently here. Where this specification and exp_001 disagree on an era boundary, exp_001 is correct and this specification has a bug.

parameters.missing_data_policy: A month missing from any of the three regions is dropped from the pooled statistic for that era in every region, and the dropped count is reported. Series are never forward-filled. The emerging file carries the -99.99 sentinel for RMW and CMA in its earliest years; the manifest records the last such cell as 1992-06, which precedes every era here, and the experiment reports the realised dropped count rather than trusting that.

pooling.alignment: A pooled cell uses the months in which ALL THREE regions are observed within the era, intersected. No series is forward-filled and no month is imputed. The count of months dropped by the intersection is reported for every pooled cell; on the frozen eras it is expected to be zero, and a non-zero count is a finding.
alternatives_reported_but_not_in_the_fal: a two-region pool of developed-ex-US and emerging only, which is the genuinely independent look at the US result
the US region alone, which must reproduce exp_001
pooling.rationale: One vote per region. The object under test is how many independent looks three regions actually supply, and any weighting fitted to the data would answer a different question. Equal weighting is also the only choice that does not require a regional market-capitalisation series this repository does not have.

also_report: the realised power to detect the 2.0 percentage-point materiality threshold, per region and pooled
the realised power to detect 0.55% per month gross, Harvey, Liu and Zhu's (2016) structural estimate of the mean return of a genuinely true factor, which is 6.6 percentage points per year
the same MDE recomputed from the HAC standard error rather than sigma/sqrt(T)
the pooled MDE and the pooled effective sample size, which are the decisive outputs of the whole experiment
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true annualised premium that a test of the given size would reject the null for with probability power_target, given the realised volatility and length: MDE_monthly = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sigma / sqrt(T), annualised by 12. Identical to exp_001, so the figures are directly comparable to its grid.

primary_grid.dependence_warning: These 27 tests are strongly dependent in two directions at once. Across regions, the three cells of one factor and era are the same construction on the same accounting variables applied to disjoint but globally correlated universes. Across eras, `recent` is nested inside `full_post_publication` for every factor, and `first_post_publication` is nested inside it too. Across factors, RMW and CMA share every era. Benjamini-Hochberg treats them as independent, so the corrected p-values are a LOWER BOUND on the true correction, and Holm-Bonferroni is reported because it is valid under arbitrary dependence.
primary_grid.description: The predeclared multiple-testing family: 3 factors x 3 regions x 3 era roles = 27 cells. Fixing the family before the run is what stops the correction from being applied to whichever subset survives. The `common_period` era is deliberately NOT a role here: for RMW and CMA it is the identical window to `full_post_publication`, and a family containing a test twice is not a family.

regional_data_availability_check.claim_under_test: Experiment 001's stated reason for skipping regional data is that "the regional files start 1990-07 and 1989-07, so they are shorter than the post-publication windows already shown to be underpowered."
regional_data_availability_check.enforcement: The experiment asserts, from the loaded series and not from this text, that every region's first observation is at or before the start of every era it is asked to evaluate, and ABORTS if it is not. A silently truncated regional window would look exactly like a shorter one.
regional_data_availability_check.finding: That reason is FALSE for the eras that matter, and the experiment must verify it against the committed manifests at run time rather than assert it. HML's post-publication era begins 1994-01 and RMW's and CMA's begin 2014-01. The developed-ex-US file begins 1990-07 and the emerging file 1989-07, so both begin before both boundaries and the regional post-publication windows are exactly as long as the US ones. The statement is true only of the ORIGINAL-SAMPLE eras, which begin 1963-07 and which this experiment excludes for precisely that reason.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: HML, RMW and CMA are already long-short spreads in every regional file. RF is NOT subtracted from any of them, in any region. Ken French defines every region's MARKET factor against the US one-month Treasury bill, but that concerns Mkt-RF and not the long-short spreads this experiment reads; no market factor enters any statistic here.

second_moment_uncertainty.application_rule: Carried through every statistic that divides by a volatility - the Sharpe ratio, the minimum detectable effect and therefore branch (b) - and reported as a SEPARATE band, never combined with a sampling interval. For a pooled statistic the band is propagated by rescaling the US leg's deviations by (1 +/- u) and recomputing, since a relative error u in the US volatility is exactly a scale error of that size on that leg. Where a conclusion would flip inside the band, the output must say so explicitly.
second_moment_uncertainty.regional_statement: The developed-ex-US and emerging files were NEVER gated against any printed table. Their second moments are UNMEASURED, which is a weaker statement than a band of zero and must be reported as such rather than as agreement. No band is quoted for them because none has been established.

us_band.finding: The Phase 1 ingestion gate is UNRESOLVED, not passed. It qualifies the effective sample size, and a finding that the regions crash together must be reported beside the pooled MDE_80 rather than buried, because it means the pooled number is an upper bound on the independent evidence rather than a measurement of it.
reported: the worst calendar year of every regional and pooled cell, and whether it is the same year across regions
the named year 2009 evaluated in every region and pooled, by name

the ten worst months of the pooled composite over the full post-publication era, and for each of them how many of the three regions were also negative in that month, against the unconditional rate at which a region is negative

the mean pairwise cross-region correlation computed on the worst decile of pooled composite months, beside the same correlation computed on all months. A tail correlation materially above the unconditional one is direct evidence that the regions crash together and therefore that the effective sample size measured over all months OVERSTATES the independent evidence available in the tail.
crash_state_dependence.why: This is the momentum-specific test and it is predeclared here so that it cannot be fitted afterwards. Daniel and Moskowitz (2016), "Momentum crashes", Journal of Financial Economics 122(2) 221-247, show that momentum crashes are state-dependent: they occur in market rebounds following bear markets, when the short leg has become a portfolio of high-beta distressed stocks. Bear markets and their rebounds are GLOBAL events. If the three regional momentum series crash in the same months, then they are markedly fewer than three independent looks precisely in the tail that decides whether the premium is worth holding, and an average correlation computed over all months will understate that.
crash_state_dependence.why_that_year: Experiment 001 measured UMD's worst post-publication rolling year in the US as -56.6% over 2008-12..2009-11, the momentum crash Daniel and Moskowitz study. The calendar year 2009 is named here in advance and evaluated in every region, so the test cannot be chosen after seeing which year turned out worst.

cross_region_bootstrap.method: Draw one set of stationary-bootstrap time indices of shape (n_resamples, months) with the frozen mean block length, and apply THE SAME row of indices to all three regional series at once. Because the composite is a fixed linear combination of contemporaneous regional observations, resampling the composite series with those indices is algebraically identical to resampling the panel and then compositing, and the implementation uses that identity. This experiment REUSES exp_005's implementation of it rather than writing a second one.
cross_region_bootstrap.the_error_it_avoids: Resampling each region with its own independent index draw. That destroys the contemporaneous correlation, makes the composite behave like an average of three independent samples, and narrows the interval by a factor that grows with the true correlation. exp_005 measured that factor at about 1.5 for HML and found a cell where the invalid procedure manufactured significance outright. The independent version IS computed and reported beside the joint one, labelled invalid.
cross_region_bootstrap.what_it_preserves: Contemporaneous cross-region dependence, and short-range serial dependence within each region.

definitions_all_reported.reading: The number of independent regions the three actually amount to. Equals 3 under zero correlation and equal variances, and 1 under perfect correlation. Computed from the realised sample covariance over the era, not assumed.
The pooled evidence expressed in independent single-region months, ignoring serial dependence. Directly comparable to the observation count of an Experiment 001 cell.
The same quantity with serial dependence in the composite folded in. This is the honest measure and is expected to be the smallest of the three.
What treating the three regions as independent samples would claim. The ratio of this to the effective figures is the size of the error this experiment exists to avoid, and it is reported explicitly.

effective_sample_size.mde_definition: MDE_80 = 12 * (z_0.95 + z_0.80) * standard_error_of_the_monthly_mean, identical to exp_001 and exp_005. It is reported from the conventional standard error sigma/sqrt(T) of the composite AND from the composite's HAC standard error.
effective_sample_size.prior_from_exp_005: exp_005 measured effective region counts of 1.49 (HML), 2.26 (RMW) and 1.76 (CMA), and the best pooled MDE_80 across all nine of its pooled cells was 2.62 pp/yr, above the 2.0 pp/yr threshold. Decision 0005 records that floor as a property of the available data. UMD's volatility is roughly 45% higher than HML's in the US post-publication window (16.55 against 11.43), and the MDE is proportional to volatility, so a pooled UMD MDE_80 comfortably above 2.0 pp/yr is the PRIOR EXPECTATION here. Stating it in advance is what makes branch (b) firing uninformative on its own and branch (a) firing the surprising outcome; it does not license reading the result before it exists.
effective_sample_size.which_one_the_falsifier_reads: Branch (b) reads the CONVENTIONAL pooled MDE_80, which is the more generous of the two because it ignores autocorrelation. Firing branch (b) on the generous reading is a fortiori, and the HAC figure is reported beside it so that a reader can see how much more generous it was.
effective_sample_size.why: This is the decisive measurement of the experiment, as it was of exp_005. Three regions of T months each supply 3T independent region-months only if the regions are uncorrelated. They are not, and how far short they fall is the number that decides branch (b).

episode_concentration.consequence: Clause a5 of the falsifier reads this. A pooled premium that does not survive dropping its own best calendar year cannot advance.
reported:
the calendar-year contribution to every regional and pooled premium
the best calendar year of every regional and pooled cell, and the premium after it is dropped
whether the best calendar year is the SAME year across regions, which is the direct test of whether the regions share an upside episode
the episode exp_001 named for UMD, the calendar year 1999, evaluated in every region BY NAME rather than by whichever year turned out best
episode_concentration.why: Experiment 001 found 79% of HML's US post-publication premium in the single year 2000 and measured UMD's own concentration: dropping UMD's best calendar year, 1999, took its US full post-publication premium from +4.19 to +3.46 pp/yr, which made UMD the least concentrated of the four factors on the upside. A premium that lives in one calendar year is a description of that year, and three regions that share the same episode are not three independent looks.

The publication record that justifies each boundary is in exp_001_factor_decay.yaml under parameters.publication_record and is inherited unchanged rather than restated here, so that it has exactly one canonical home.

pooling.alignment: A pooled cell uses the months in which ALL THREE regions are observed within the era, intersected. No series is forward-filled and no month is imputed. The count of months dropped by the intersection is reported for every pooled cell; on the frozen eras it is expected to be zero, and a non-zero count is a finding.
alternatives_reported_but_not_in_the_fal: a two-region pool of developed-ex-US and emerging only, which is the genuinely independent look at the US result
the US region alone, which must reproduce exp_001
pooling.rationale: One vote per region, identical to exp_005. The object under test is how many independent looks three regions actually supply, and any weighting fitted to the data would answer a different question. Equal weighting is also the only choice that does not require a regional market-capitalisation series this repository does not have.

also_report:
the realised power to detect the 2.0 percentage-point materiality threshold, per region and pooled
the realised power to detect 0.55% per month gross, Harvey, Liu and Zhu's (2016) structural estimate of the mean return of a genuinely true factor, which is 6.6 percentage points per year
the same MDE recomputed from the HAC standard error rather than sigma/sqrt(T)
the pooled MDE and the pooled effective sample size, which are the decisive outputs of the whole experiment
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true annualised premium that a test of the given size would reject the null for with probability power_target, given the realised volatility and length: MDE_monthly = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sigma / sqrt(T), annualised by 12. Identical to exp_001 and exp_005, so the figures are directly comparable to both grids.

primary_grid.dependence_warning: These 9 tests are strongly dependent in two directions at once. Across regions, the three cells of one era are the same 30/70 prior-return construction applied to disjoint but globally correlated universes. Across eras, `recent` is nested inside `full_post_publication` and so is `first_post_publication`. Benjamini-Hochberg treats them as independent, so the corrected p-values are a LOWER BOUND on the true correction, and Holm-Bonferroni is reported because it is valid under arbitrary dependence.
primary_grid.description: The predeclared multiple-testing family: 1 factor x 3 regions x 3 era roles = 9 cells. Fixing the family before the run is what stops the correction from being applied to whichever subset survives. The `common_period` era is deliberately NOT a role here: exp_005 excluded it for the same reason and UMD's common-period cell is already in exp_001's family.

regional_data_availability_check.claim_under_test: Experiment 005 stated that UMD "could not be tested because no regional momentum file exists in this repository", and docs/research/ factor-persistence.md printed the stronger and false form of it.
regional_data_availability_check.enforcement: The experiment asserts, from the loaded series and not from this text, that every region's first observation is at or before the start of every era it is asked to evaluate, and ABORTS if it is not. A silently truncated regional window would look exactly like a shorter one.
regional_data_availability_check.finding: The narrow claim was true of the repository and the broad one is FALSE of the data. Ken French publishes three regional momentum files. The developed-ex-US file begins 1990-11 and the emerging file 1990-01, both before UMD's 1994-01 post-publication boundary, so the regional post-publication windows are exactly as long as the US one. Both begin later than the corresponding five-factor file because a 2-12 month prior return cannot be formed until twelve months of history exist.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: UMD is already a long-short spread in every regional file: it is the average of two high-prior-return portfolios minus the average of two low-prior-return portfolios. RF is NOT subtracted from it, in any region. Subtracting a bill rate from a zero-investment spread would move every mean by the bill rate and is a category error.

second_moment_uncertainty.consequence_for_branch_b: Branch (b) reads the pooled MDE_80, which is proportional to the composite's volatility. exp_005 could bound the effect of its band because the band was measured. Here it cannot be bounded at all, which is reported as an unquantified sensitivity rather than omitted.
second_moment_uncertainty.regional_statement: Every volatility, Sharpe ratio and minimum detectable effect in this experiment rests on a second moment that was never checked against any published table, in every region. The output must say so beside every one of them and must not quote a band it does not have.
second_moment_uncertainty.unmeasured_not_zero: The 0.0 above is a numerical placeholder for "no band to apply", NOT a measurement. The Phase 1 ingestion gate covered the US five-factor file and HML and RMW within it. NO momentum file, in ANY region, has ever been gated against a printed table in this repository. All three second moments are therefore UNMEASURED, which is a weaker statement than a band of zero and must be reported as such rather than as agreement. exp_001 said exactly this about the US momentum file and this specification extends it to all three.

source_pin.policy: All three files are pinned by the sha256 of their raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current source vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download, and a premium computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one.

microcap_investability.why: Hou, Xue and Zhang (2020) put microcaps at 3.2% of market capitalisation and 60.7% of the stock count, and attribute much of the anomaly literature to them. power.note: Power is reported for the SPREADS, in percentage points per year. primary_definitions.description: The predeclared family of five. Clause (1) of the falsifier reads the spread of their POINT ESTIMATES. Fixing the family before the run is what stops the spread from being computed over whichever subset is widest.

family.reading: THE PRIMARY. The value tilt held at the same 50/50 size weighting as its own benchmark, so the difference is book-to-market and nothing else.

What a retail investor holding this instead of a total-market fund would have received. Contains a large size tilt as well as a value tilt, and that is exactly why it is in the family rather than replacing the primary.
The closest public analogue of a large-capitalisation value fund held instead of a total-market fund. The most implementable member of the family.
The value tilt inside the large-capitalisation universe alone.
The small-value corner in its 2x3 form, held instead of a total-market fund. Expected to be the least implementable member and is reported as such regardless of what it measures.

reported_but_outside_the_family.why_excluded: It is exactly half of value_halves_vs_market by construction, so including it would widen the spread by arithmetic rather than by evidence. It is reported because real funds are not 100% tilted and a reader needs to see that the capture scales linearly with the tilt.

identities.checked_against: the HML column of french_us_ff5, and of french_us_ff3
identities.tolerance_rationale: The portfolio file prints two decimal places in percent, so each of the four terms carries up to 0.005 percentage points of rounding. Half a printed digit on the assembled spread is 0.005 percentage points, which is 0.00005 in decimal, and that is the tolerance.

identities.checked_against: the SMB column of french_us_ff3 ONLY. It will NOT reconcile against french_us_ff5, whose SMB averages the size legs of the book-to-market, profitability and investment sorts. Both checks are run and the five-factor disagreement is REPORTED as the expected finding it is, because a reader who assumed the two SMBs were the same series would draw a false conclusion from this experiment.

identities.tolerance_rationale: One and a half printed digits rather than one. The momentum sort is reconstituted monthly and its file and the factor file are rounded independently, so the same four-term rounding argument gives a slightly wider bound. Stated in advance rather than widened later.

reconstruction_identities.why: These are the integration test and clause (0) of the rejection rule. If the published factor cannot be rebuilt from the published portfolios, then the long legs read here are not the legs of the factor measured elsewhere in this repository, and every capture fraction is a ratio of two unrelated things.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: The six portfolios are TOTAL returns, not excess returns, so the market comparator must also be a total return: Mkt-RF + RF from the same file and vintage. Subtracting a market factor that is already net of the bill from a long-only total return would understate the long-only leg by the entire Treasury bill rate, which over 1963-07..2025-12 is several percentage points a year and would flatter every capture fraction in this experiment. The size-neutral benchmark is a total return already, so no bill enters it and none is subtracted. For the regional files RF is the US one-month bill in every region, exactly as Ken French defines it; the regional markets are USD and unhedged.

source_pin.policy: Every file is pinned by the sha256 of its raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current source vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download.

parameters.spread_threshold_rationale: Three quarters of the 0.40 under test. The rule is that a multiplier whose benchmark-driven range covers three quarters of its own assumed value cannot be used as a multiplier, because substituting a defensible alternative benchmark would move the edge-budget line it feeds by more than the line is worth. The threshold is a function of 0.40 alone and of no observed quantity.

Subtracting a market factor that is already net of the bill from a long-only total return would understate the long-only leg by the entire Treasury bill rate, which over 1963-07..2025-12 is several percentage points a year and would flatter every capture fraction in this experiment. The size-neutral benchmark is a total return already, so no bill enters it and none is subtracted. For the regional files RF is the US one-month bill in every region, exactly as Ken French defines it; the regional markets are USD and unhedged.

source_pin.policy: Every file is pinned by the sha256 of its raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current source vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download.

parameters.spread_threshold_rationale: Three quarters of the 0.40 under test. The rule is that a multiplier whose benchmark-driven range covers three quarters of its own assumed value cannot be used as a multiplier, because substituting a defensible alternative benchmark would move the edge-budget line it feeds by more than the line is worth. The threshold is a function of 0.40 alone and of no observed quantity.
