notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_008_managed_futures

annualisation.mean: multiply the monthly arithmetic mean by 12
annualisation.note: sqrt(12) assumes serial independence, which monthly returns violate. The HAC standard error is reported precisely because that assumption is wrong, and the two are always shown side by side.
annualisation.ratio: A capture fraction is a ratio of two monthly means and is therefore already annualisation-invariant: multiplying both by 12 leaves it unchanged. It is computed from monthly means and the invariance is asserted in a test rather than assumed.
annualisation.volatility: multiply the monthly standard deviation by sqrt(12)

inherited: the era names hml_original_sample, hml_first_post_publication, hml_full_post_publication, recent, umd_original_sample and umd_full_post_publication, with both boundaries unchanged
the publication record and boundary justifications, by reference
the 2.0 percentage-point-per-year materiality threshold
the 80% power target and the closed-form minimum detectable effect
the frozen 12-month mean block length and its 6 and 24 month neighbours
the 10000 resample count and the 0.10 Benjamini-Hochberg alpha
the sample end of 2025-12 and the holdout beyond it
not_inherited: the RMW and CMA eras, which this experiment does not test
the cost_model.applied = false of both, because a long-only portfolio is close enough to holdable that refusing to price it would be an evasion rather than a discipline
inherited_from_exp_001_and_005.rule: Nothing inherited may be re-derived differently here. Where this specification and exp_001 disagree on an era boundary, exp_001 is correct and this specification has a bug. The experiment asserts the shared boundaries against exp_001's own file at run time.

microcap_investability.measured_from: The 5x5 file's own "Number of Firms in Portfolios" and "Average Market Cap" tables. The share of capitalisation in a cell is (firms * average cap) / sum over cells of the same product. That ratio is INVARIANT to the average-cap table's scale, which the file never states and which data/french.py therefore records as unknown. No absolute capitalisation figure is reported, because none can be.
reported: firm count and capitalisation share of every 5x5 cell, at the last month of the primary era and averaged over it
the same for the whole ME1 size quintile
the corner recomputed with ME1 dropped, and the difference
microcap_investability.verdict_required: The output must state plainly whether the small-value corner is implementable at retail given what those shares turn out to be. A number without that sentence is not an answer to the question that was asked.
microcap_investability.why: Hou, Xue and Zhang (2020) put microcaps at 3.2% of market capitalisation and 60.7% of the stock count, and attribute much of the anomaly literature to them. If the small-value corner lives in cells that hold a fifth of the listed companies and a fraction of a percent of the money, then the corner is not a thing a retail investor can hold in size, whatever its measured premium.

parameters.missing_data_policy: A month missing from any series entering a statistic is dropped from that statistic, and the dropped count is reported. Series are never forward-filled. The -99.99 and -999 sentinels are converted to missing by the parser before any arithmetic, and the validation report is checked for sentinel leakage before any statistic is computed.

power.definition: MDE_80 = 12 * (z_0.95 + z_0.80) * standard_error_of_the_monthly_mean, identical to exp_001 and exp_005, so the figures are directly comparable to their grids. Reported from the conventional standard error and from the HAC standard error, side by side.
power.note: Power is reported for the SPREADS, in percentage points per year. It is not reported for the capture fractions, because the null there is 0.40 rather than zero and a minimum detectable effect against a non-zero null of a ratio with a shared denominator would be a misleading statistic. The interval is the honest summary for the ratios and it is what the falsifier reads.

primary_definitions.description: The predeclared family of five. Clause (1) of the falsifier reads the spread of their POINT ESTIMATES. Fixing the family before the run is what stops the spread from being computed over whichever subset is widest.

family.reading: THE PRIMARY. The value tilt held at the same 50/50 size weighting as its own benchmark, so the difference is book-to-market and nothing else.

What a retail investor holding this instead of a total-market fund would have received. Contains a large size tilt as well as a value tilt, and that is exactly why it is in the family rather than replacing the primary.
The closest public analogue of a large-capitalisation value fund held instead of a total-market fund. The most implementable member of the family.
The value tilt inside the large-capitalisation universe alone.
The small-value corner in its 2x3 form, held instead of a total-market fund. Expected to be the least implementable member and is reported as such regardless of what it measures.

reported_but_outside_the_family.what: 0.5 * (Mkt-RF + RF) + 0.5 * 0.5 * (SH + BH), against the market
reported_but_outside_the_family.why_excluded: It is exactly half of value_halves_vs_market by construction, so including it would widen the spread by arithmetic rather than by evidence. It is reported because real funds are not 100% tilted and a reader needs to see that the capture scales linearly with the tilt.

reported_but_outside_the_family.what: ((SL + SM + SH + BL + BM + BH) / 6 - 0.5 * (SL + BL)) / HML
reported_but_outside_the_family.why_excluded: It is the SHORT leg's share, not a long-only tilt. It is reported because it must sum with the primary to 1 by construction, which is a second integration test of the arithmetic and of the claim that the primary is near one half for structural rather than empirical reasons.

reported_but_outside_the_family.what: 0.5 * (ME1 BM5 + ME5 BM5) from the 5x5 file, against the market
the same, against the equal-weighted average of all 25 cells
SMALL HiBM from the 5x5 file, against the market
the same corner computation with the ME1 size quintile DROPPED entirely, using ME2 as the small leg
reported_but_outside_the_family.why: The direct test of whether the small-value result depends on the smallest quintile. It is predeclared so that it cannot be run only if the headline figure needs defending.

reported_but_outside_the_family.what: 0.5 * (SHiPRIOR + BHiPRIOR) against the equal-weighted six
the same, against the market

the small-capitalisation quintile and decile of Portfolios_Formed_on_ME against the market, and the long-short size spread they imply, which is the premium test the design map records as never having been run
value_halves_vs_size_neutral and value_halves_vs_market computed on the developed-ex-US and emerging 2x3 files against their own regional market and their own regional HML

identities.checked_against: the HML column of french_us_ff5, and of french_us_ff3
identities.tolerance_rationale: Propagated, not guessed. The portfolio file prints two decimal places in percent, so each of the four terms carries a rounding error of at most 0.005 percentage points. The identity weights all four terms by 0.5, so the sum of the absolute weights is 2 and the reconstruction inherits at most 2 * 0.005 = 0.010 percentage points. The published HML column is itself printed to two decimal places, contributing a further 0.005. The bound is 0.015 percentage points per month, which is 0.00015 in decimal. See the correction record at the top of this file: an earlier version of this specification declared 0.00005 here on a wrong derivation, and that error is on the ledger.

identities.checked_against: the SMB column of french_us_ff3 ONLY. It will NOT reconcile against french_us_ff5, whose SMB averages the size legs of the book-to-market, profitability and investment sorts. Both checks are run and the five-factor disagreement is REPORTED as the expected finding it is, because a reader who assumed the two SMBs were the same series would draw a false conclusion from this experiment.
identities.tolerance_rationale: The same propagation as the HML identity. The size identity weights six terms by one third, so the sum of the absolute weights is 2 exactly as before, and the bound is the same 0.015 percentage points per month.

Identical in structure to the HML identity and therefore identical in value: four terms weighted by 0.5, absolute weights summing to 2, at most 0.005 percentage points of rounding each, plus 0.005 for the independently rounded Mom column, giving 0.015 percentage points per month. An earlier version of this specification declared 0.000075 here on a wrong derivation and that error fired clause (0) on the first run; see the correction record at the top of this file.

reconstruction_identities.why: These are the integration test and clause (0) of the rejection rule. If the published factor cannot be rebuilt from the published portfolios, then the long legs read here are not the legs of the factor measured elsewhere in this repository, and every capture fraction is a ratio of two unrelated things.

parameters.risk_free_treatment: The six portfolios are TOTAL returns, not excess returns, so the market comparator must also be a total return: Mkt-RF + RF from the same file and vintage. Subtracting a market factor that is already net of the bill from a long-only total return would understate the long-only leg by the entire Treasury bill rate, which over 1963-07..2025-12 is several percentage points a year and would flatter every capture fraction in this experiment. The size-neutral benchmark is a total return already, so no bill enters it and none is subtracted. For the regional files RF is the US one-month bill in every region, exactly as Ken French defines it; the regional markets are USD and unhedged.

source_pin.policy: Every file is pinned by the sha256 of its raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS rather than producing a graded result. Ken French rebuilds the entire history from the current source vintage on every rebuild, so a changed hash is a new vintage, not a corrupt download.

parameters.spread_threshold_rationale: Three quarters of the 0.40 under test. The rule is that a multiplier whose benchmark-driven range covers three quarters of its own assumed value cannot be used as a multiplier, because substituting a defensible alternative benchmark would move the edge-budget line it feeds by more than the line is worth. The threshold is a function of 0.40 alone and of no observed quantity.

annualisation.mean: multiply the monthly arithmetic mean by 12
annualisation.note: sqrt(12) assumes serial independence, which monthly returns violate. The HAC standard error is reported precisely because that assumption is wrong, and the two are always shown side by side.
annualisation.ratio: A capture fraction is a ratio of two monthly means and is therefore already annualisation-invariant: multiplying both by 12 leaves it unchanged. It is computed from monthly means and the invariance is asserted in a test rather than assumed.
annualisation.volatility: multiply the monthly standard deviation by sqrt(12)

inherited: the era names hml_original_sample, hml_first_post_publication, hml_full_post_publication, recent, umd_original_sample and umd_full_post_publication, with both boundaries unchanged
the publication record and boundary justifications, by reference
the 2.0 percentage-point-per-year materiality threshold
the 80% power target and the closed-form minimum detectable effect
the frozen 12-month mean block length and its 6 and 24 month neighbours
the 10000 resample count and the 0.10 Benjamini-Hochberg alpha
the sample end of 2025-12 and the holdout beyond it
not_inherited: the RMW and CMA eras, which this experiment does not test
the cost_model.applied = false of both, because a long-only portfolio is close enough to holdable that refusing to price it would be an evasion rather than a discipline
inherited_from_exp_001_and_005.rule: Nothing inherited may be re-derived differently here. Where this specification and exp_001 disagree on an era boundary, exp_001 is correct and this specification has a bug. The experiment asserts the shared boundaries against exp_001's own file at run time.

microcap_investability.measured_from: The 5x5 file's own "Number of Firms in Portfolios" and "Average Market Cap" tables. The share of capitalisation in a cell is (firms * average cap) / sum over cells of the same product. That ratio is INVARIANT to the average-cap table's scale, which the file never states and which data/french.py therefore records as unknown. No absolute capitalisation figure is reported, because none can be.
reported: firm count and capitalisation share of every 5x5 cell, at the last month of the primary era and averaged over it
the same for the whole ME1 size quintile
the corner recomputed with ME1 dropped, and the difference
microcap_investability.verdict_required: The output must state plainly whether the small-value corner is implementable at retail given what those shares turn out to be. A number without that sentence is not an answer to the question that was asked.
microcap_investability.why: Hou, Xue and Zhang (2020) put microcaps at 3.2% of market capitalisation and 60.7% of the stock count, and attribute much of the anomaly literature to them. If the small-value corner lives in cells that hold a fifth of the listed companies and a fraction of a percent of the money, then the corner is not a thing a retail investor can hold in size, whatever its measured premium.

notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_007_longonly_capture

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_warning: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) would divide every standard error by 3.46 and shrink far too little, which is the direction that manufactures skill.
alpha_shrinkage.source: Fama and French (2010) bootstrap of US active equity mutual funds, 1984-2006. TRANSFERRED, NOT MEASURED: it comes from active equity funds and is applied here to managed-futures ETFs, a different population in a different asset class. It decides every shrunk number and its transfer is a stated assumption.

aqr_source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS. AQR reconstructs the full history each time the returns are updated, so an unrecognised hash is a new vintage rather than a corrupted download, and a tracking difference computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one.

aqr_tsmom_tracking.role: primary. exposure delivery against the benchmark Experiment 004 measured.

ff5_umd.role: The standard equity model, included so that the multiple-testing family is every fund times every specification estimated and not only the one reported. A loading that appears in one specification and not the others is a specification artefact.

static_exposure_set.role: Experiment 004's decisive set, unchanged. Goyal and Jegadeesh (2018) show time-series momentum carries a large embedded time-varying market position; this is the specification under which an intercept-stripped replica delivered 44% of the index's marginal benefit. Running it on the products asks whether they are anything more than that.

parameters.cash_rate: The one-month Treasury bill from the SAME Ken French file as the factors, so that every intercept is interpretable as an alpha against the rate Mkt-RF is defined against.
parameters.clause_d_disclosure: Realised distributions and prospectus after-tax returns were read from sponsor documents while the product facts were assembled, BEFORE any N-PORT return was downloaded but AFTER they were visible to the author. Any threshold on them chosen now would be a threshold chosen after seeing the quantity. They are therefore measured and reported and are in NO falsifier clause. This is recorded as a limitation rather than repaired by inventing a bar.

correction_log.evidence: The refused run aborted inside the clause (d) block, before any result object was constructed, before any artifact was written and before any `results_viewed` entry existed. No number from Experiment 008 had been seen when this correction was made. Neither the replica nor the residual value moved, and no threshold, criterion or clause was touched.
correction_log.reason: The first frozen value carried invented digits. The write-up of Experiment 004 prints +1.342 to three decimals and the remaining digits were supplied from nothing rather than read from the artifact. The verification guard described in `policy` refused the run at a drift of 0.00057 pp/yr, which is exactly what it exists to do, and the ledgered `failed` entry for run b718e47b014049eebc80a296ffe9f4b5 records the refusal. The corrected value is read from Experiment 004's artifact.

clause_d_rerun.policy: The three quantities above are quoted from Experiment 004's ledgered artifact so that this decision is reproducible from Git alone, because artifacts are not in Git. When the artifact is present it is read and the quoted values are VERIFIED against it; a mismatch beyond the tolerance is a finding and aborts. Experiment 004's own specification, ledger entries and status are not touched by anything here. Its result stands as recorded; this is a second, differently-specified look at the same decision, and the ledger shows both.
clause_d_rerun.what: PART B. A re-run of Experiment 004's DECISION, not of its data. Experiment 004's frozen falsifier clause (d) reads "an attribution on static asset exposures plus a volatility-scaled market position leaves a marginal benefit below the materiality threshold, i.e. a simpler static exposure explains it". That sentence admits an ABSOLUTE reading (the replica's own marginal benefit clears 0.30 pp/yr, so reject) and a RELATIVE reading (the sleeve's margin over the replica clears 0.30 pp/yr, so retain). Experiment 004 applied the absolute reading as frozen and said in its own write-up that the relative reading gives `unresolved`. Both verdicts are computed here, side by side, from the numbers Experiment 004 ledgered.

parameters.criteria_order_note: Applied in this fixed order, and only the FIRST failure is recorded, which is what makes the funnel add up. A fund below the asset floor is never looked up for a fee, so a missing fee cannot masquerade as a screen decision -- the gathering gap Experiment 002 had to repair mid-flight.
parameters.exposure_not_alpha: EXPOSURE DELIVERY AND ALPHA ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND ONLY ONE IS ANSWERABLE HERE. Exposure delivery is a loading and a difference of means against a named benchmark, and 45 to 78 months can measure it. Alpha is a small residual mean, and the minimum detectable alpha at 80% power on a window this short is larger than any plausible true alpha. Every reported intercept is shrunk by the fund's OWN factor computed from its OWN standard error, is printed beside its raw value and its detection threshold, and is never quoted alone. Experiment 002 measured a median realised shrinkage factor of 0.431 on index funds against the framework's 0.121 reference; the factor is measured here too and never hardcoded.

french_source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS, for the same reason.

parameters.inception_rationale: Three complete calendar years must exist inside the window, which is the least a fixed-halves stability test can be run on. It is the criterion that excludes the 2023-2025 launches, and it excludes them for a stated reason rather than because they looked bad.
parameters.maximum_net_expense_ratio_rationale: Two and a half times Experiment 002's 0.60% ceiling, because a futures programme with a Cayman subsidiary genuinely costs more to run than an index equity fund. The ceiling exists to keep the audit on the exchange-traded shelf rather than to grade cost: a fund that clears it is not thereby cheap, and the realised fee of every passing fund is reported.
parameters.minimum_net_assets_rationale: One tenth of Experiment 002's billion-dollar floor. The listed managed-futures shelf is an order of magnitude smaller than the listed factor shelf, and a billion-dollar floor would leave two funds. Every fund below the floor is still recorded with its assets so a reader can see exactly what a lower floor would have admitted.

screening_patterns.pattern_provenance: Both patterns were written by reading SERIES NAMES ONLY in the two censuses, before any return was downloaded and with the data sets' return tables never opened. A name carries no performance, so a pattern tuned on names cannot be tuned on results. The exclusion pattern removes single-asset-class, sector, size-segment, allocation, income, leveraged and inverse products; it is the reason "Fidelity Trend Fund", a 1958 large-cap growth fund, and "Pacer Trendpilot US Large Cap ETF", an equity-and-cash rotation, are not in this audit.

notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_008_managed_futures

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) understates the standard error by 3.46 and shrinks far too little, which is the direction that manufactures skill.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. With true gross alpha normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010) and a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed with shrinkage_factor = 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + SE^2), recomputed from each fund's OWN standard error.

parameters.maximum_net_expense_ratio_rationale: Identical to Experiment 002, so that "expensive" means the same thing in both audits even though the ex-US shelf is dearer.
parameters.minimum_monthly_observations_rationale: A six-factor regression plus an intercept spends seven degrees of freedom, so 36 months is the point below which a HAC standard error at six lags stops meaning anything. It is NOT a claim that 36 months is enough to identify a loading; the minimum detectable effect reported per fund is the statement about that, and for most funds it is large.
parameters.minimum_net_assets_rationale: Half of Experiment 002's floor. Chosen from the COUNT of qualifying series at each level, which is visible in the census before any return is downloaded and never from performance: at Experiment 002's 1,000 million the ex-US screen returns 23 series and at 500 million it returns 39, and the question this experiment exists to answer includes whether the shelf is deep enough to matter. Using the US floor would have answered that question by assumption.

us_pedestal_only.used_for: The VTI pedestal alone, so that the ex-US structural drag is a difference between two pedestals estimated on the same months rather than a comparison against a number published from a different window.

primary.what: The fund's own monthly total return for each month of the reporting period, filed on Form NPORT-P per share class, in percent, already net of the fund's fees and of foreign dividend withholding.
primary.why_it_is_still_exploratory: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, the figures are fund-reported and unaudited, General Instruction G lets each filer use its own methodology, and for the ex-US shelf most histories are shorter still. Decision 0002 is NOT overturned.
primary.why_this_and_not_a_price_feed: Decision 0002 found that no free PRICE feed documents a total-return contract, a corporate-action policy, delisting coverage or a revision history. Form N-PORT is a signed regulatory disclosure of a defined statistic, permanently archived, in which a correction is a separate document and the original stays readable.

secondary.status: EXPLORATORY and not research-grade, per decision 0002. No result depends on it. Where it is unavailable the check is recorded as not run.
secondary.used_for: An independent cross-check over the same months, and nothing else.

changes.change: The mandate pattern requires a REGION word and a FACTOR word. Experiment 002 required a factor word and its exclusion pattern removed every region word.
changes.why: The two screens are complements over the same census, so a fund can appear in at most one of them and no fund can appear in both.

changes.change: A `us_overlap` criterion excludes any fund whose name claims a mandate including the United States -- an explicit US token outside an `ex-US` qualifier, or global/world/ACWI with no `ex-US` qualifier at all.
changes.why: A fund holding US stocks cannot be priced by a non-US factor panel. The `ex-US` qualifier is stripped before the US token is looked for; without that, "Hartford Multifactor Developed Markets (ex-US) ETF" would exclude itself.

changes.change: A `region_in_map` criterion admits only developed_ex_us and emerging.
changes.why: Ken French publishes those two files and nothing between them. A world-ex-US fund holds both in proportions this repository cannot observe.

changes.change: The frame is the union of the 2019Q4 and 2025Q4 censuses.
changes.why: Every product the question is about launched after 2019. A 2019Q4-only frame would have excluded AVDV, AVIV, AVES, DISV, DFIV and DFEV by construction. This follows Experiment 008, which faced the same problem with DBMF, KMLM and CTA.

changes.change: Experiment 002's `inception_on_or_before: 2016-12-31` criterion is not applied. It is replaced by a per-fund reported sample length and minimum detectable effect.
changes.why: The cutoff exists so an audit is not measuring a launch. Applied here it would delete the entire modern ex-US small-value shelf, which is the subject of the experiment. Short history is reported as a finding instead of being screened away, and no fund is rejected for it.

changes.change: 500 million USD rather than 1,000 million, on the maximum of two censuses.
changes.why: Chosen from census counts visible before any return: 23 series clear 1,000 million and 39 clear 500 million. Whether the shelf is deep is part of the question.

changes.change: Attrition classifies a qualifying series absent from the later census as a death and a qualifying series still filing under a non-qualifying name as a rename.
changes.effect_on_published_us_results: Experiment 002's published attrition figure is computed the naive way and is therefore an OVERSTATEMENT of deaths by however many renames it contains. This experiment recomputes that decomposition under Experiment 002's own patterns and reports both numbers. It changes no loading, tracking difference or verdict in Experiment 002; it corrects the interpretation of one survivorship diagnostic.
changes.why: Differencing name-qualified identifier sets counts a rename as a death. Every iShares "Edge" product dropped that word inside the window.

screen_changes_from_exp_002.description: Exactly what differs from Experiment 002's screen, why, and what it does to the published US numbers. Experiment 002's own module, specification, committed universe and results are UNTOUCHED; this experiment asserts its two regexes byte-for-byte before running and aborts if either has moved.

screening_patterns.mandate_pattern_note: Ordered; the FIRST match wins, so "International Small Cap Value" is small-cap value rather than small-cap or value. Derived from the official series name so the criterion needs no sponsor document and cannot be revised while reading one. The sponsor-stated mandate is recorded separately and every disagreement is reported.
screening_patterns.world_ex_us_regex: all[- ]?world|world ex|all international|total international|acwi ex|global ex|all[- ]?country

unobservable_in_the_primary_source:
Realised taxable distributions and their split between qualified dividend, ordinary income and capital gain. Form N-PORT reports one total return.
Portfolio turnover, which lives in the annual report on Form N-CSR as unstructured HTML.
Foreign tax paid and foreign tax credit passed through to shareholders, which is reported on Form 1099-DIV box 7 and in the annual report, not in Form N-PORT. This is the single most important ex-US-specific gap and it is recorded rather than estimated.
Securities-lending revenue split, which is disclosed by sponsor policy rather than per fund per year in this source and is already inside net asset value.

validation_gates.cross_source_gate: Where both sources have a month, the median absolute difference between the N-PORT and secondary monthly returns is reported per fund. A large disagreement is a finding about the data, reported rather than reconciled.
validation_gates.market_beta_gate: Each regional comparator's regression on its own Mkt-RF must produce a beta within 0.10 of 1.00 and an R-squared of at least 0.93, for the same reasons and with the same looser thresholds.
validation_gates.month_alignment: Item B.5 reports rtn1 as the FIRST month of the reporting period and rtn3 as the month ending on repPdDate. A reversed reading would shift every history by two months while leaving the numbers plausible, so alignment is CHECKED against an independent series rather than assumed.
validation_gates.regional_market_gate: VEA's reconstructed series must correlate at least 0.97 with the French developed-ex-US market total return and VWO's at least 0.95 with the emerging one, and both must show their largest single-month loss in 2020-03. The thresholds are LOOSER than Experiment 002's 0.99 for VTI, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: no investable ex-US fund is the French research portfolio. FTSE and MSCI classify Korea, Poland and Canada differently from Ken French, the investable indices exclude the smallest deciles the research portfolios include, and the fund's return is net of withholding while the research portfolio's construction is undocumented on that point. A gate tight enough for a US total-market fund would fail here for reasons that are about index definitions rather than about the data path.

us_pedestal_only.used_for: The VTI pedestal alone, so that the ex-US structural drag is a difference between two pedestals estimated on the same months rather than a comparison against a number published from a different window.

primary.what: The fund's own monthly total return for each month of the reporting period, filed on Form NPORT-P per share class, in percent, already net of the fund's fees and of foreign dividend withholding.
primary.why_it_is_still_exploratory: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, the figures are fund-reported and unaudited, General Instruction G lets each filer use its own methodology, and for the ex-US shelf most histories are shorter still. Decision 0002 is NOT overturned.
primary.why_this_and_not_a_price_feed: Decision 0002 found that no free PRICE feed documents a total-return contract, a corporate-action policy, delisting coverage or a revision history. Form N-PORT is a signed regulatory disclosure of a defined statistic, permanently archived, in which a correction is a separate document and the original stays readable.

secondary.status: EXPLORATORY and not research-grade, per decision 0002. No result depends on it. Where it is unavailable the check is recorded as not run.
secondary.used_for: An independent cross-check over the same months, and nothing else.

changes.change: The mandate pattern requires a REGION word and a FACTOR word. Experiment 002 required a factor word and its exclusion pattern removed every region word.
changes.why: The two screens are complements over the same census, so a fund can appear in at most one of them and no fund can appear in both.

changes.change: A `us_overlap` criterion excludes any fund whose name claims a mandate including the United States -- an explicit US token outside an `ex-US` qualifier, or global/world/ACWI with no `ex-US` qualifier at all.
changes.why: A fund holding US stocks cannot be priced by a non-US factor panel. The `ex-US` qualifier is stripped before the US token is looked for; without that, "Hartford Multifactor Developed Markets (ex-US) ETF" would exclude itself.

changes.change: A `region_in_map` criterion admits only developed_ex_us and emerging.
changes.why: Ken French publishes those two files and nothing between them. A world-ex-US fund holds both in proportions this repository cannot observe.

changes.change: The frame is the union of the 2019Q4 and 2025Q4 censuses.
changes.why: Every product the question is about launched after 2019. A 2019Q4-only frame would have excluded AVDV, AVIV, AVES, DISV, DFIV and DFEV by construction. This follows Experiment 008, which faced the same problem with DBMF, KMLM and CTA.

changes.change: Experiment 002's `inception_on_or_before: 2016-12-31` criterion is not applied. It is replaced by a per-fund reported sample length and minimum detectable effect.
changes.why: The cutoff exists so an audit is not measuring a launch. Applied here it would delete the entire modern ex-US small-value shelf, which is the subject of the experiment. Short history is reported as a finding instead of being screened away, and no fund is rejected for it.

changes.change: 500 million USD rather than 1,000 million, on the maximum of two censuses.
changes.why: Chosen from census counts visible before any return: 23 series clear 1,000 million and 39 clear 500 million. Whether the shelf is deep is part of the question.

changes.change: Attrition classifies a qualifying series absent from the later census as a death and a qualifying series still filing under a non-qualifying name as a rename.
changes.effect_on_published_us_results: Experiment 002's published attrition figure is computed the naive way and is therefore an OVERSTATEMENT of deaths by however many renames it contains. This experiment recomputes that decomposition under Experiment 002's own patterns and reports both numbers. It changes no loading, tracking difference or verdict in Experiment 002; it corrects the interpretation of one survivorship diagnostic.
changes.why: Differencing name-qualified identifier sets counts a rename as a death. Every iShares "Edge" product dropped that word inside the window.

screen_changes_from_exp_002.description: Exactly what differs from Experiment 002's screen, why, and what it does to the published US numbers. Experiment 002's own module, specification, committed universe and results are UNTOUCHED; this experiment asserts its two regexes byte-for-byte before running and aborts if either has moved.

screening_patterns.mandate_pattern_note: Ordered; the FIRST match wins, so "International Small Cap Value" is small-cap value rather than small-cap or value. Derived from the official series name so the criterion needs no sponsor document and cannot be revised while reading one. The sponsor-stated mandate is recorded separately and every disagreement is reported.
screening_patterns.world_ex_us_regex: all[- ]?world|world ex|all international|total international|acwi ex|global ex|all[- ]?country

unobservable_in_the_primary_source:
Realised taxable distributions and their split between qualified dividend, ordinary income and capital gain. Form N-PORT reports one total return.
Portfolio turnover, which lives in the annual report on Form N-CSR as unstructured HTML.
Foreign tax paid and foreign tax credit passed through to shareholders, which is reported on Form 1099-DIV box 7 and in the annual report, not in Form N-PORT. This is the single most important ex-US-specific gap and it is recorded rather than estimated.
Securities-lending revenue split, which is disclosed by sponsor policy rather than per fund per year in this source and is already inside net asset value.

validation_gates.cross_source_gate: Where both sources have a month, the median absolute difference between the N-PORT and secondary monthly returns is reported per fund. A large disagreement is a finding about the data, reported rather than reconciled.
validation_gates.market_beta_gate: Each regional comparator's regression on its own Mkt-RF must produce a beta within 0.10 of 1.00 and an R-squared of at least 0.93, for the same reasons and with the same looser thresholds.
validation_gates.month_alignment: Item B.5 reports rtn1 as the FIRST month of the reporting period and rtn3 as the month ending on repPdDate. A reversed reading would shift every history by two months while leaving the numbers plausible, so alignment is CHECKED against an independent series rather than assumed.
validation_gates.regional_market_gate: VEA's reconstructed series must correlate at least 0.97 with the French developed-ex-US market total return and VWO's at least 0.95 with the emerging one, and both must show their largest single-month loss in 2020-03. The thresholds are LOOSER than Experiment 002's 0.99 for VTI, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: no investable ex-US fund is the French research portfolio. FTSE and MSCI classify Korea, Poland and Canada differently from Ken French, the investable indices exclude the smallest deciles the research portfolios include, and the fund's return is net of withholding while the research portfolio's construction is undocumented on that point. A gate tight enough for a US total-market fund would fail here for reasons that are about index definitions rather than about the data path.

base_weights.rationale: A frozen, round approximation of global equity market capitalisation, not an optimisation. The exact split is not load-bearing: the credit depends on beta to the core, and the three regional markets correlate above 0.7 with each other, so a reasonable reweighting moves sigma_p by well under a percentage point. That claim is checked as a hostile test rather than asserted.

parameters.cash_series_rationale: TB3MS is the monthly average secondary-market three-month Treasury bill rate on a discount basis: the conventional monthly cash proxy in the US asset-pricing literature and the series exp_004 froze, so cash is the same asset in both experiments. DGS3MO and DFF are registered in this repository and were NOT used; they are different maturities on different constructions. Ken French's own RF column is used to turn Mkt-RF into a total return, because that is the only sum that reconstructs the market's total return, and is not used as the cash asset.

correlation_sensitivity.definition: credit_term = 12 * gamma * (sigma_fp - rho_ip * sigma_i * sigma_p), so d(credit)/d(rho_ip) = -12 * gamma * sigma_i * sigma_p. Report the derivative per 0.10 of correlation, and the credit re-evaluated at both ends of the correlation's own block-bootstrap 95% interval with the volatilities held at their point estimates.
correlation_sensitivity.rationale: A credit of a few tens of basis points that moves by more than itself when the correlation moves by 0.10 is not a finding. The samples here cannot pin a correlation tightly, and that has to be visible in the output rather than inferred from it.

decomposition.fixture_policy: The decomposition is a pure function of five scalars and is intended to be checked against a closed form derived independently of this implementation. If an independently derived closed form disagrees with these numbers, the closed form wins until proven otherwise, and the disagreement is a finding rather than a tolerance to loosen.
decomposition.identity: For portfolio p, sleeve i and funding leg f, funding weight w of i out of f: dg/dw|_{w=0} = E[(r_i - r_f)/(1 + r_p)] exactly, and to second order in the moments = (mu_i - mu_f) - (sigma_ip - sigma_fp). With f = p the second term is sigma_p^2 (1 - beta_ip), the diversification credit. For a CRRA investor with risk aversion gamma the same expansion gives (mu_i - mu_f) - gamma * (sigma_ip - sigma_fp), and gamma = 1 recovers the growth case.
decomposition.why_both: The exact derivative is the true first-order effect on the growth rate and needs no distributional assumption. The two-moment decomposition is what SPLITS that effect into the standalone term and the credit. Reporting only the split would hide how much of it the two moments actually capture; reporting only the exact figure would answer the wrong question. The residual between them is reported so a reader can see the approximation error rather than trust it.

evaluation_disclosure.statement: This experiment evaluates published research portfolios, one vendor series and one modelled proxy. Ken French's files are paper portfolios rebuilt from the current CRSP or Bloomberg vintage on every release and carry no trading cost, no capacity limit and no borrow. The AQR series is maintained by a firm that sells the strategy. The long-duration sleeve is modelled from a yield and is not a total-return history at all. No figure here is an achievable investor outcome, and no write-up may describe one as such.
evaluation_disclosure.what_would_make_this_confirmatory: Investable total-return histories with a documented corporate-action contract, a walk-forward weight-selection rule fitted only on data before each evaluation window, and a cost model calibrated to executed trades rather than assumed. None of the three exists in this repository today.

parameters.flatness_definition: The certainty-equivalent surface is reported on the whole weight grid. Three flatness statistics accompany every optimum: the width of the plateau on which the gain is at least 90% of its maximum; the gain at the cap as a fraction of the gain at the optimum; and the width of the region on which the gain exceeds the materiality threshold. A large optimal weight sitting on a wide plateau is not evidence that the weight is large; it is evidence that the data cannot locate a weight.
parameters.materiality_rationale: The same threshold exp_004 froze, so that a marginal figure from this experiment is directly comparable with the one from that one. It is a threshold on the NET marginal certainty equivalent, not on a gross premium.

also_report: the realised marginal figure as a multiple of its own minimum detectable effect
the number of months and the effective number of independent 12-month blocks
the minimum detectable effect on the diversification credit alone
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true marginal certainty-equivalent gain that a one-sided test of size alpha would reject the null for with probability power_target. Two forms are reported for every sleeve and neither is allowed to stand alone: MDE_bootstrap = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sd(bootstrap replicates of the marginal figure), which carries the serial dependence and the nonlinearity of the certainty equivalent; and MDE_normal = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * 12 * sigma_d / sqrt(T) on the monthly incremental return d_t, which is the form exp_001 and exp_005 report and is included so the figures are comparable with theirs.

predeclared_prediction.how_it_is_scored: Per sleeve, record predicted sign of the credit, realised sign, and whether the realised credit's correlation-sensitivity band excludes the predicted sign. Report the tally.
predeclared_prediction.statement: Because beta_ip = rho_ip * sigma_i / sigma_p, an equity sleeve's higher volatility is expected to more than offset its correlation being below one. Worked example at plausible numbers: rho = 0.88, sigma_i = 20%, sigma_p = 15% gives beta = 1.173 and a credit of 2.25% * (1 - 1.173) = -0.39 percentage points per year. The prediction is therefore that every long-only equity sleeve -- small-value, regional equity, long-only momentum -- shows a beta at or above one to the equity core and a credit at or below zero, and that only trend and the long-duration proxy show a positive credit. This is recorded so that the result can CONTRADICT it. A contradiction is the more interesting outcome and must be reported at least as loudly as a confirmation.

parameters.sample_start_rationale: 1991-01 is the first January on or after the latest first observation among the eleven monthly inputs. Developed ex-US momentum begins 1990-11, which is the binding constraint; a momentum factor needs twelve months of prior returns before it can be formed, so the regional momentum files start later than the five-factor files. The window is exactly 35 whole calendar years = 420 months, which is required because the certainty equivalent is computed from non-overlapping calendar-year gross returns and a partial year cannot be silently dropped.

sleeves_not_tested.reason: NOT TESTED. No research-grade gold price or total-return series is reachable. Decision record 0002 governs; no gold series is registered in portfolio_edge.data.fred and no free price feed may be substituted. Gold is one of only two candidate assets with a plausibly low equity beta, so its absence biases this experiment toward finding no credit anywhere, and that direction is stated rather than left for a reader to notice.

NOT TESTED. Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, giving at most about 78 months of common history. The minimum-detectable-effect arithmetic in parameters.power shows what that buys, and it is not enough to distinguish a 0.30 percentage-point marginal effect from zero. exp_002 and exp_008 already use N-PORT for what it can answer, which is what funds hold and what they charge, not whether a sleeve adds growth.
NOT TESTED as an investable series. Decision record 0002. The modelled GS10 duration proxy stands in its place and is forced to `unresolved` by falsifier clause (u5).

fred.note: robustness arm only; feeds the modelled long-duration proxy, which is not research grade

source_pin.policy: Every French and AQR input is pinned by the sha256 of its raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS. base_weights.rationale: A frozen, round approximation of global equity market capitalisation, not an optimisation. The exact split is not load-bearing: the credit depends on beta to the core, and the three regional markets correlate above 0.7 with each other, so a reasonable reweighting moves sigma_p by well under a percentage point. That claim is checked as a hostile test rather than asserted.

parameters.cash_series_rationale: TB3MS is the monthly average secondary-market three-month Treasury bill rate on a discount basis: the conventional monthly cash proxy in the US asset-pricing literature and the series exp_004 froze, so cash is the same asset in both experiments. DGS3MO and DFF are registered in this repository and were NOT used; they are different maturities on different constructions. Ken French's own RF column is used to turn Mkt-RF into a total return, because that is the only sum that reconstructs the market's total return, and is not used as the cash asset.

correlation_sensitivity.definition: credit_term = 12 * gamma * (sigma_fp - rho_ip * sigma_i * sigma_p), so d(credit)/d(rho_ip) = -12 * gamma * sigma_i * sigma_p. Report the derivative per 0.10 of correlation, and the credit re-evaluated at both ends of the correlation's own block-bootstrap 95% interval with the volatilities held at their point estimates.
correlation_sensitivity.rationale: A credit of a few tens of basis points that moves by more than itself when the correlation moves by 0.10 is not a finding. The samples here cannot pin a correlation tightly, and that has to be visible in the output rather than inferred from it.

decomposition.fixture_policy: The decomposition is a pure function of five scalars and is intended to be checked against a closed form derived independently of this implementation. If an independently derived closed form disagrees with these numbers, the closed form wins until proven otherwise, and the disagreement is a finding rather than a tolerance to loosen.
decomposition.identity: For portfolio p, sleeve i and funding leg f, funding weight w of i out of f: dg/dw|_{w=0} = E[(r_i - r_f)/(1 + r_p)] exactly, and to second order in the moments = (mu_i - mu_f) - (sigma_ip - sigma_fp). With f = p the second term is sigma_p^2 (1 - beta_ip), the diversification credit. For a CRRA investor with risk aversion gamma the same expansion gives (mu_i - mu_f) - gamma * (sigma_ip - sigma_fp), and gamma = 1 recovers the growth case.
decomposition.why_both: The exact derivative is the true first-order effect on the growth rate and needs no distributional assumption. The two-moment decomposition is what SPLITS that effect into the standalone term and the credit. Reporting only the split would hide how much of it the two moments actually capture; reporting only the exact figure would answer the wrong question. The residual between them is reported so a reader can see the approximation error rather than trust it.

evaluation_disclosure.statement: This experiment evaluates published research portfolios, one vendor series and one modelled proxy. Ken French's files are paper portfolios rebuilt from the current CRSP or Bloomberg vintage on every release and carry no trading cost, no capacity limit and no borrow. The AQR series is maintained by a firm that sells the strategy. The long-duration sleeve is modelled from a yield and is not a total-return history at all. No figure here is an achievable investor outcome, and no write-up may describe one as such.
evaluation_disclosure.what_would_make_this_confirmatory: Investable total-return histories with a documented corporate-action contract, a walk-forward weight-selection rule fitted only on data before each evaluation window, and a cost model calibrated to executed trades rather than assumed. None of the three exists in this repository today.

parameters.flatness_definition: The certainty-equivalent surface is reported on the whole weight grid. Three flatness statistics accompany every optimum: the width of the plateau on which the gain is at least 90% of its maximum; the gain at the cap as a fraction of the gain at the optimum; and the width of the region on which the gain exceeds the materiality threshold. A large optimal weight sitting on a wide plateau is not evidence that the weight is large; it is evidence that the data cannot locate a weight.
parameters.materiality_rationale: The same threshold exp_004 froze, so that a marginal figure from this experiment is directly comparable with the one from that one. It is a threshold on the NET marginal certainty equivalent, not on a gross premium.

also_report: the realised marginal figure as a multiple of its own minimum detectable effect
the number of months and the effective number of independent 12-month blocks
the minimum detectable effect on the diversification credit alone
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true marginal certainty-equivalent gain that a one-sided test of size alpha would reject the null for with probability power_target. Two forms are reported for every sleeve and neither is allowed to stand alone: MDE_bootstrap = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sd(bootstrap replicates of the marginal figure), which carries the serial dependence and the nonlinearity of the certainty equivalent; and MDE_normal = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * 12 * sigma_d / sqrt(T) on the monthly incremental return d_t, which is the form exp_001 and exp_005 report and is included so the figures are comparable with theirs.

predeclared_prediction.how_it_is_scored: Per sleeve, record predicted sign of the credit, realised sign, and whether the realised credit's correlation-sensitivity band excludes the predicted sign. Report the tally.
predeclared_prediction.statement: Because beta_ip = rho_ip * sigma_i / sigma_p, an equity sleeve's higher volatility is expected to more than offset its correlation being below one. Worked example at plausible numbers: rho = 0.88, sigma_i = 20%, sigma_p = 15% gives beta = 1.173 and a credit of 2.25% * (1 - 1.173) = -0.39 percentage points per year. The prediction is therefore that every long-only equity sleeve -- small-value, regional equity, long-only momentum -- shows a beta at or above one to the equity core and a credit at or below zero, and that only trend and the long-duration proxy show a positive credit. This is recorded so that the result can CONTRADICT it. A contradiction is the more interesting outcome and must be reported at least as loudly as a confirmation.

parameters.sample_start_rationale: 1991-01 is the first January on or after the latest first observation among the eleven monthly inputs. Developed ex-US momentum begins 1990-11, which is the binding constraint; a momentum factor needs twelve months of prior returns before it can be formed, so the regional momentum files start later than the five-factor files. The window is exactly 35 whole calendar years = 420 months, which is required because the certainty equivalent is computed from non-overlapping calendar-year gross returns and a partial year cannot be silently dropped.

sleeves_not_tested.reason: NOT TESTED. No research-grade gold price or total-return series is reachable. Decision record 0002 governs; no gold series is registered in portfolio_edge.data.fred and no free price feed may be substituted. Gold is one of only two candidate assets with a plausibly low equity beta, so its absence biases this experiment toward finding no credit anywhere, and that direction is stated rather than left for a reader to notice.

NOT TESTED. Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, giving at most about 78 months of common history. The minimum-detectable-effect arithmetic in parameters.power shows what that buys, and it is not enough to distinguish a 0.30 percentage-point marginal effect from zero. exp_002 and exp_008 already use N-PORT for what it can answer, which is what funds hold and what they charge, not whether a sleeve adds growth.
NOT TESTED as an investable series. Decision record 0002. The modelled GS10 duration proxy stands in its place and is forced to `unresolved` by falsifier clause (u5).

fred.note: robustness arm only; feeds the modelled long-duration proxy, which is not research grade

source_pin.policy: Every French and AQR input is pinned by the sha256 of its raw bytes AND by the sha256 of the derived table, and a mismatch ABORTS. Both sources rebuild their entire history in place on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a new vintage rather than a corrupt download, and a marginal figure computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. FRED appends rather than rewrites, so its hashes are recorded and reported without aborting.

parameters.weight_cap_rationale: A satellite sleeve inside a diversified portfolio. Twenty per cent is the largest weight a single non-core sleeve plausibly takes; ten per cent is the hostile arm. Both were chosen before any result and neither is optimised.

notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_010_marginal_sleeve_value

alpha_shrinkage.annualisation_trap: An annual alpha is TWELVE times a monthly intercept, so its standard error annualises by x12 and never by sqrt(12). Using sqrt(12) understates the standard error by 3.46 and shrinks far too little, which is the direction that manufactures skill.
alpha_shrinkage.description: Every alpha is shrunk before it means anything. With true gross alpha normal with mean zero and cross-sectional standard deviation 1.25%/yr (Fama and French 2010) and a single-fund standard error SE, the posterior mean is shrinkage_factor * observed with shrinkage_factor = 1.25^2 / (1.25^2 + SE^2), recomputed from each fund's OWN standard error.

parameters.maximum_net_expense_ratio_rationale: Identical to Experiment 002, so that "expensive" means the same thing in both audits even though the ex-US shelf is dearer.
parameters.minimum_monthly_observations_rationale: A six-factor regression plus an intercept spends seven degrees of freedom, so 36 months is the point below which a HAC standard error at six lags stops meaning anything. It is NOT a claim that 36 months is enough to identify a loading; the minimum detectable effect reported per fund is the statement about that, and for most funds it is large.
parameters.minimum_net_assets_rationale: Half of Experiment 002's floor. Chosen from the COUNT of qualifying series at each level, which is visible in the census before any return is downloaded and never from performance: at Experiment 002's 1,000 million the ex-US screen returns 23 series and at 500 million it returns 39, and the question this experiment exists to answer includes whether the shelf is deep enough to matter. Using the US floor would have answered that question by assumption.

us_pedestal_only.used_for: The VTI pedestal alone, so that the ex-US structural drag is a difference between two pedestals estimated on the same months rather than a comparison against a number published from a different window.

primary.what: The fund's own monthly total return for each month of the reporting period, filed on Form NPORT-P per share class, in percent, already net of the fund's fees and of foreign dividend withholding.
primary.why_it_is_still_exploratory: Public N-PORT filings begin in 2019, the figures are fund-reported and unaudited, General Instruction G lets each filer use its own methodology, and for the ex-US shelf most histories are shorter still. Decision 0002 is NOT overturned.
primary.why_this_and_not_a_price_feed: Decision 0002 found that no free PRICE feed documents a total-return contract, a corporate-action policy, delisting coverage or a revision history. Form N-PORT is a signed regulatory disclosure of a defined statistic, permanently archived, in which a correction is a separate document and the original stays readable.

secondary.status: EXPLORATORY and not research-grade, per decision 0002. No result depends on it. Where it is unavailable the check is recorded as not run.
secondary.used_for: An independent cross-check over the same months, and nothing else.

changes.change: The mandate pattern requires a REGION word and a FACTOR word. Experiment 002 required a factor word and its exclusion pattern removed every region word.
changes.why: The two screens are complements over the same census, so a fund can appear in at most one of them and no fund can appear in both.

changes.change: A `us_overlap` criterion excludes any fund whose name claims a mandate including the United States -- an explicit US token outside an `ex-US` qualifier, or global/world/ACWI with no `ex-US` qualifier at all.
changes.why: A fund holding US stocks cannot be priced by a non-US factor panel. The `ex-US` qualifier is stripped before the US token is looked for; without that, "Hartford Multifactor Developed Markets (ex-US) ETF" would exclude itself.

changes.change: A `region_in_map` criterion admits only developed_ex_us and emerging.
changes.why: Ken French publishes those two files and nothing between them. A world-ex-US fund holds both in proportions this repository cannot observe.

changes.change: The frame is the union of the 2019Q4 and 2025Q4 censuses.
changes.why: Every product the question is about launched after 2019. A 2019Q4-only frame would have excluded AVDV, AVIV, AVES, DISV, DFIV and DFEV by construction. This follows Experiment 008, which faced the same problem with DBMF, KMLM and CTA.

changes.change: Experiment 002's `inception_on_or_before: 2016-12-31` criterion is not applied. It is replaced by a per-fund reported sample length and minimum detectable effect.
changes.why: The cutoff exists so an audit is not measuring a launch. Applied here it would delete the entire modern ex-US small-value shelf, which is the subject of the experiment. Short history is reported as a finding instead of being screened away, and no fund is rejected for it.

changes.change: 500 million USD rather than 1,000 million, on the maximum of two censuses.
changes.why: Chosen from census counts visible before any return: 23 series clear 1,000 million and 39 clear 500 million. Whether the shelf is deep is part of the question.

changes.change: Attrition classifies a qualifying series absent from the later census as a death and a qualifying series still filing under a non-qualifying name as a rename.
changes.effect_on_published_us_results: Experiment 002's published attrition figure is computed the naive way and is therefore an OVERSTATEMENT of deaths by however many renames it contains. This experiment recomputes that decomposition under Experiment 002's own patterns and reports both numbers. It changes no loading, tracking difference or verdict in Experiment 002; it corrects the interpretation of one survivorship diagnostic.
changes.why: Differencing name-qualified identifier sets counts a rename as a death. Every iShares "Edge" product dropped that word inside the window.

screen_changes_from_exp_002.description: Exactly what differs from Experiment 002's screen, why, and what it does to the published US numbers. Experiment 002's own module, specification, committed universe and results are UNTOUCHED; this experiment asserts its two regexes byte-for-byte before running and aborts if either has moved.

screening_patterns.mandate_pattern_note: Ordered; the FIRST match wins, so "International Small Cap Value" is small-cap value rather than small-cap or value. Derived from the official series name so the criterion needs no sponsor document and cannot be revised while reading one. The sponsor-stated mandate is recorded separately and every disagreement is reported.
screening_patterns.world_ex_us_regex: all[- ]?world|world ex|all international|total international|acwi ex|global ex|all[- ]?country

unobservable_in_the_primary_source:
Realised taxable distributions and their split between qualified dividend, ordinary income and capital gain. Form N-PORT reports one total return.
Portfolio turnover, which lives in the annual report on Form N-CSR as unstructured HTML.
Foreign tax paid and foreign tax credit passed through to shareholders, which is reported on Form 1099-DIV box 7 and in the annual report, not in Form N-PORT. This is the single most important ex-US-specific gap and it is recorded rather than estimated.
Securities-lending revenue split, which is disclosed by sponsor policy rather than per fund per year in this source and is already inside net asset value.

validation_gates.cross_source_gate: Where both sources have a month, the median absolute difference between the N-PORT and secondary monthly returns is reported per fund. A large disagreement is a finding about the data, reported rather than reconciled.
validation_gates.market_beta_gate: Each regional comparator's regression on its own Mkt-RF must produce a beta within 0.10 of 1.00 and an R-squared of at least 0.93, for the same reasons and with the same looser thresholds.
validation_gates.month_alignment: Item B.5 reports rtn1 as the FIRST month of the reporting period and rtn3 as the month ending on repPdDate. A reversed reading would shift every history by two months while leaving the numbers plausible, so alignment is CHECKED against an independent series rather than assumed.
validation_gates.regional_market_gate: VEA's reconstructed series must correlate at least 0.97 with the French developed-ex-US market total return and VWO's at least 0.95 with the emerging one, and both must show their largest single-month loss in 2020-03. The thresholds are LOOSER than Experiment 002's 0.99 for VTI, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: no investable ex-US fund is the French research portfolio. FTSE and MSCI classify Korea, Poland and Canada differently from Ken French, the investable indices exclude the smallest deciles the research portfolios include, and the fund's return is net of withholding while the research portfolio's construction is undocumented on that point. A gate tight enough for a US total-market fund would fail here for reasons that are about index definitions rather than about the data path.

attribution.rationale: Goyal and Jegadeesh (2018) show the strategy carries a large embedded net-long market position and that adding a time-varying market position to a cross-sectional strategy reproduces the time-series result. The decisive test is therefore whether a static market exposure plus a volatility-scaled market position reproduces the sleeve. The absolute market term is a convexity proxy: a strategy that is genuinely long crisis convexity should load positively on it. The lagged market term captures the slow signal.
attribution.replica_caveat: The replica is fitted on the same sample it is evaluated on, so its marginal benefit is an UPPER bound. That is the conservative direction for this test: it makes clause (d) of the falsifier easier to fire, which is correct, because the question is whether a simpler exposure COULD explain the result.

bond_proxy.construction: A ten-year Treasury total return reconstructed from FRED GS10 by the standard duration-and-convexity approximation on a par bond: r_t = y_{t-1}/12 - D_t (y_t - y_{t-1}) + 0.5 C_t (y_t - y_{t-1})^2, with D_t and C_t the modified duration and convexity of a ten-year par bond at y_{t-1}.
bond_proxy.used_as: declared robustness arm only, never the primary benchmark
bond_proxy.warning: This is a MODELLED series, not an investable total-return history. It has no documented total-return contract, no coupon reinvestment convention and no transaction costs. It exists so that the 2022 window, in which equities and bonds fell together, is not silently removed from the experiment by the absence of a bond leg. No conclusion may rest on it alone.

parameters.cash_series_rationale: TB3MS is the monthly average secondary-market three-month Treasury bill rate on a discount basis: the conventional monthly cash proxy in the US asset-pricing literature, at the same monthly frequency as every other series here, and the series against which the vendor's "excess return" is most nearly defined. DGS3MO and DFF are registered in this repository and were NOT used: DGS3MO is a daily constant-maturity interpolated yield on a different basis and DFF is an overnight interbank rate with no three-month maturity. Swapping them moves a Sharpe ratio, so the choice is declared here and not revisited after seeing a result.

concretisation_log.change: passive_benchmark changed from "60/40 equity/bond from investable total-return histories" to 60% Ken French US market total return / 40% FRED TB3MS cash.
concretisation_log.reason: Decision record 0002: no free price source is research-grade and no investable bond total-return history is available. The equity/bond form is preserved as parameters.bond_proxy, a declared robustness arm built from a modelled GS10 duration approximation and flagged research_grade false.

concretisation_log.change: volatility_lookback_days retained at 60 and translated to a monthly exponentially weighted centre of mass of 60/21 months.
concretisation_log.reason: The public vendor series is monthly, so the vendor's own daily 60-day exponentially weighted estimator is not computable from it. The recovered methodology text confirms 60 days is the vendor's centre of mass, so the frozen number was right and only its frequency had to change.

concretisation_log.change: The execution-delay hostile test changed from "one and five additional trading days" to one additional MONTH.
concretisation_log.reason: A monthly series cannot express a one- or five-day delay. One month is the smallest implementable delay and is strictly more hostile than either frozen value, so the substitution cannot flatter the result.

concretisation_log.change: Source pins added with the sha256 of every input actually used.
concretisation_log.reason: The vendor reconstructs its full history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a new vintage and must abort rather than silently change every number.

parameters.crisis_window_note: Frozen before any result is examined and defined by peak-to-trough equity drawdown dates, not by when the sleeve performed well.

evaluation_disclosure.author_interest: The series is maintained by a firm that sells the strategy. This is not an accusation; it is a recorded conflict that raises the required evidential standard.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: This experiment evaluates a published, author-maintained vendor series. It is NOT an independent replication of time-series momentum. An independent reimplementation would require contract-level futures histories, roll conventions, collateral returns, execution assumptions and point-in-time market availability, none of which are inputs here. Any write-up that describes this as a replication is wrong, and the archived workbook, sheet, and revision date must accompany every figure because vendor URLs, workbooks and revisions change.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS the experiment. AQR reconstructs its full history on every update and Ken French rebuilds his from each new CRSP vintage, so an unrecognised hash is a new vintage rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. FRED hashes change whenever a new observation is appended, so the FRED pins are recorded and reported but do NOT abort; the abort applies to the two sources whose history is rewritten in place.

volatility_estimator.form: Exponentially weighted variance of lagged returns with the centre of mass stated in the vendor's own recovered methodology text: sigma_t^2 = k * sum_i (1-delta) delta^i (r_{t-1-i} - rbar_t)^2 with delta / (1 - delta) = the centre of mass, and k the annualisation factor.
volatility_estimator.this_repository_form: The public series is MONTHLY, so a daily estimator is not computable from it. The identical exponentially weighted form is applied to monthly returns at the same calendar centre of mass, days / 21, with k = 12. The 60-, 20- and 120-day lookbacks become 2.857, 0.952 and 5.714 months. This is an approximation of the vendor's estimator, not the vendor's estimator, and the frozen day-based values are retained above so that the translation stays visible.
volatility_estimator.vendor_form: The vendor applies this to DAILY returns with a 60-day centre of mass and k = 261, and uses the estimate at t-1 on the returns at t. Both facts come from text recovered from the workbook's embedded picture, not from cells.

correlation_sensitivity.definition: credit_term = 12 * gamma * (sigma_fp - rho_ip * sigma_i * sigma_p), so d(credit)/d(rho_ip) = -12 * gamma * sigma_i * sigma_p. Report the derivative per 0.10 of correlation, and the credit re-evaluated at both ends of the correlation's own block-bootstrap 95% interval with the volatilities held at their point estimates.
correlation_sensitivity.rationale: A credit of a few tens of basis points that moves by more than itself when the correlation moves by 0.10 is not a finding. The samples here cannot pin a correlation tightly, and that has to be visible in the output rather than inferred from it.

decomposition.fixture_policy: The decomposition is a pure function of five scalars and is intended to be checked against a closed form derived independently of this implementation. If an independently derived closed form disagrees with these numbers, the closed form wins until proven otherwise, and the disagreement is a finding rather than a tolerance to loosen.
decomposition.identity: For portfolio p, sleeve i and funding leg f, funding weight w of i out of f: dg/dw|_{w=0} = E[(r_i - r_f)/(1 + r_p)] exactly, and to second order in the moments = (mu_i - mu_f) - (sigma_ip - sigma_fp). With f = p the second term is sigma_p^2 (1 - beta_ip), the diversification credit. For a CRRA investor with risk aversion gamma the same expansion gives (mu_i - mu_f) - gamma * (sigma_ip - sigma_fp), and gamma = 1 recovers the growth case.
decomposition.why_both: The exact derivative is the true first-order effect on the growth rate and needs no distributional assumption. The two-moment decomposition is what SPLITS that effect into the standalone term and the credit. Reporting only the split would hide how much of it the two moments actually capture; reporting only the exact figure would answer the wrong question. The residual between them is reported so a reader can see the approximation error rather than trust it.

parameters.flatness_definition: The certainty-equivalent surface is reported on the whole weight grid. Three flatness statistics accompany every optimum: the width of the plateau on which the gain is at least 90% of its maximum; the gain at the cap as a fraction of the gain at the optimum; and the width of the region on which the gain exceeds the materiality threshold. A large optimal weight sitting on a wide plateau is not evidence that the weight is large; it is evidence that the data cannot locate a weight.
parameters.materiality_rationale: The same threshold exp_004 froze, so that a marginal figure from this experiment is directly comparable with the one from that one. It is a threshold on the NET marginal certainty equivalent, not on a gross premium.

also_report: the realised marginal figure as a multiple of its own minimum detectable effect
the number of months and the effective number of independent 12-month blocks
the minimum detectable effect on the diversification credit alone
power.definition: The minimum detectable effect is the smallest true marginal certainty-equivalent gain that a one-sided test of size alpha would reject the null for with probability power_target. Two forms are reported for every sleeve and neither is allowed to stand alone: MDE_bootstrap = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * sd(bootstrap replicates of the marginal figure), which carries the serial dependence and the nonlinearity of the certainty equivalent; and MDE_normal = (z_{1-alpha} + z_{power}) * 12 * sigma_d / sqrt(T) on the monthly incremental return d_t, which is the form exp_001 and exp_005 report and is included so the figures are comparable with theirs.

predeclared_prediction.how_it_is_scored: Per sleeve, record predicted sign of the credit, realised sign, and whether the realised credit's correlation-sensitivity band excludes the predicted sign. Report the tally.
predeclared_prediction.statement: Because beta_ip = rho_ip * sigma_i / sigma_p, an equity sleeve's higher volatility is expected to more than offset its correlation being below one. Worked example at plausible numbers: rho = 0.88, sigma_i = 20%, sigma_p = 15% gives beta = 1.173 and a credit of 2.25% * (1 - 1.173) = -0.39 percentage points per year. The prediction is therefore that every long-only equity sleeve -- small-value, regional equity, long-only momentum -- shows a beta at or above one to the equity core and a credit at or below zero, and that only trend and the long-duration proxy show a positive credit. This is recorded so that the result can CONTRADICT it. A contradiction is the more interesting outcome and must be reported at least as loudly as a confirmation.

parameters.sample_start_rationale: 1991-01 is the first January on or after the latest first observation among the eleven monthly inputs. rejudgement.trial_count: This specification adds ZERO trials to the repository's search. It re-judges the same twelve sleeves on the same data that exp_010 already spent. Any later deflated-Sharpe or family-wise count must treat exp_010 and this file as ONE search of ten sleeves, not two searches of ten, and the Holm family here is the same family of ten by the same argument exp_010 gives.
rejudgement.what_changed: One thing: the gamma at which the deciding metric is computed, from 3 to 1. The inputs, pinned vintages, base portfolios, sleeves, funding legs, cost columns, weight grids, window, eras, block lengths, resample count and seed are all byte-identical to exp_010's. The seed is deliberately unchanged so that the two runs draw the SAME bootstrap index stream and the difference between them is the metric and nothing else.
rejudgement.what_it_may_not_do: It may not promote anything. Re-judging already-examined data is weaker evidence than a first look at it, not stronger, so the ceiling of `exploratory` that exp_010's rejection_rule imposes is inherited unchanged and a status ABOVE it is impossible whatever any sleeve measures.
rejudgement.when_it_was_decided: AFTER exp_010's numbers were read. That is the dangerous direction and it is recorded here rather than glossed. Two things bound the danger. First, the change was calibrated on the CASH CONTROL, which carries no hypothesis and cannot promote anything: it is a machine check whose correct answer was known before the data was seen. Second, the change is strictly HOSTILE to every candidate -- it removes a reward, raises the effective bar for every sleeve that was clearing it on de-risking, and moves this family's status from `unresolved` to a worse one. A metric changed after the fact that makes everything look better would be worthless; this one makes everything look worse, which is the only direction in which such a change is cheap to trust.
