evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written, frozen and hashed before the experiment module produced any statistic. The DATA, however, has been searched by fifteen earlier specifications, and the weights, the fund list and the loadings were chosen by people who had read those results. That is the look-ahead that matters here and no freezing step removes it.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every ticker in this experiment is a linear combination of public factor series and a fee. No fund's returns were used, because none is committed. The tournament therefore scores CONSTRUCTIONS. A construction result transfers to a fund only to the extent that the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost, which experiments 002, 009, 013, 014 and 015 measured for the tilt funds and which nobody has measured for MATE or JPFP.

financing_basis_band.basis: 0.62% is the point estimate Experiments 016 and 016b charge: ten equity-index futures rolls Dec-2022 to Mar-2025 against 3-month Term SOFR, recorded in `docs/research/structural-and-tax-edges.md` section 3 as of 2026-08-16. The 0.98% to 2.31% endpoints are the break-even financing band derived for a trend overlay elsewhere in this repository. The grid spans both.
financing_basis_band.reporting: Report whether the ordering of the watched wrapper arms is the same at every point of the band. IF IT IS NOT, THE RANKING OF THOSE ARMS IS NOT A FINDING and must not be presented as one. Note that the levered control carries more futures notional (0.3216) than any wrapper arm does, so a rising basis does not move every arm the same way; it charges the benchmark hardest.

fund_mapping.doctrine: ticker -> basis expression -> what the mapping assumes -> what error it introduces. Loadings are this repository's own measured values from `src/content/shelf.ts` as of 2026-08-17. A market beta of 1.000 is an assumption everywhere: no market beta was measured for any of these funds.

funds.assumes: VTI is the US market. Its measured HML of +0.0247 is carried because it is the incumbent loading every tilt is measured AGAINST, and dropping it would overstate every tilt by that amount.
funds.error: Ignores VTI's measured raw alpha of -0.547 pp/yr, which is also the US pedestal, so the two cancel and the fund sits exactly on its own model. Ignores +1.84 bp/yr of net securities lending.

funds.assumes: VXUS is 75% developed ex-US and 25% emerging by weight. THIS IS AN ASSUMPTION AND NOT A MEASUREMENT: this repository holds no global capitalisation series and `src/content/portfolios.ts` says so explicitly. Swept at 0.70/0.30 and 0.80/0.20.
funds.error: A misassigned regional weight of 5 points moves the control's return by the emerging-developed return difference times 0.05.

funds.assumes: VEA is the developed ex-US market. Loadings measured over 51 months.
funds.error: Ignores a measured raw alpha of -0.31 pp/yr, which is the developed pedestal.

funds.assumes: Loadings measured over 51 months (roughly 2021-2025) describe 1990-2026. One value cycle is longer than that window.
funds.error: THE LARGEST SINGLE MAPPING RISK IN THE TOURNAMENT. DFIV's measured raw alpha is -4.11 pp/yr against a 3.52 pp/yr detection floor, and the headline arms do not charge it. At a 10% weight, charging `alpha - pedestal` = -3.80 costs the arm 38 bp/yr. Four ex-US large-value funds read -2.2 to -4.1 and this repository does not know why. The `charge_measured_alpha` arm exists for this fund.
funds.expression: 1.000 * dxus_mkt + 0.662 * dxus_hml - 0.114 * dxus_smb - 0.001 * dxus_rmw - 0.122 * dxus_cma + 0.016 * dxus_umd

funds.assumes: Loadings measured over 51 months describe 1990-2026.
funds.error: Raw alpha -0.92 against a 5.28 floor, uncharged in the headline. The SMB leg is variance with no priced expectation: the size premium is +0.33 pp/yr against a 2.47 pp/yr floor and is not signable on any panel.

funds.assumes: Loadings measured over 77 months describe 1990-2026, and that a long-only momentum fund with 105%/yr turnover pays only its 25 bp fee.
funds.error: The turnover assumption is the weak one. At 105% annual turnover and the 0.55 bp US round-trip spread the internal trading cost is under 1 bp/yr on spread alone, but market impact is not modelled at all and momentum is the strategy where it lives. The -0.394 CMA loading is large, negative and unexplained.
funds.expression: 1.000 * dxus_mkt + 0.540 * dxus_umd + 0.218 * dxus_hml - 0.164 * dxus_smb + 0.040 * dxus_rmw - 0.394 * dxus_cma

funds.assumes: IEMG is the emerging market. No loading was measured for it.
funds.error: Ignores +9.87 bp/yr of net securities lending, the largest on the shelf.

funds.assumes: The +0.237 measured on the EMERGING panel over 51 months, not the -0.074 the same fund reads on the US panel. Choosing the panel chooses the sign, and the emerging panel is chosen because that is the panel the fund's mandate names.
funds.error: The fund is `unresolved` on this repository's own shelf: 51 months put its loading interval across the 0.15 bar. Its fee is assumed, not read.

funds.assumes: The N-PORT of 2026-04-30: SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 at 74.09% of net assets plus E-mini futures at 33.1%, giving 107.2% equity, with a government money fund at 16.04% as collateral and a trend book at roughly 294% gross notional delivering about 100% of risk exposure. The S&P 500 is mapped to the total US market.
funds.error: Substituting the total market for the S&P 500 leg adds a small-cap exposure the fund does not hold. The trend leg's mapping to AQR's TSMOM is the mapping this experiment is least able to defend: TSMOM is 58 markets, volatility-scaled to 40% per position, gross of costs, and RSST's book is not it. Sweeping the trend beta by +/-20% is the only answer this design has.

funds.assumes: Form N-PORT of 2026-05-31: an S&P 500 ETF at 50.30% of net assets plus a long E-mini S&P 500 future at 65.57%, giving a base leg of 115.87% and delta -0.159, so the wrapper keeps the whole funding-rule gap. The S&P 500 is mapped to the total US market, as RSST's leg is.
funds.error: The index future is NOT separable into base completion and the trend book's own equity position, because both sleeves trade equity-index futures and no filing tags a contract by sleeve. The contractual floor is the prospectus target of 100%, at delta 0.00, and `proposal_mate_prospectus_floor` runs that instead. Gross notional on a volatility-targeted trend book is an artefact of the risk target rather than an exposure: MATE's whole derivative book ran 339% of net assets in February and 405% in May while its stated targets did not move. No SEC-standardised after-tax table exists for it, because it has not completed a calendar year.

funds.assumes: RSST'S FILED STRUCTURE AT A FEE NO VERIFIED PRODUCT ON THIS SHELF CHARGES. Two stacked equity-plus-managed-futures ETFs post-dating the shelf audit have surfaced at a stated 0.10% net and 0.35%, and neither has been verified in `src/content/shelf.ts`. This arm exists to price the fee dimension, not to recommend a fund, and it must never be quoted as a product result.
funds.error: Everything except the 10 bp is RSST's. A net fee quoted under a waiver is not a fee: the shelf's own audit found waivers, recoupment clauses and acquired-fund fees that a stated net expense ratio omits, and none of that has been checked for these two products.

funds.assumes: THE PROSPECTUS PROSE, NOT A FILING. JPFP commenced operations on 2026-05-27 with $17.07m of net assets and has filed no Form N-PORT; its series S000101300 appears in none of the 24 filings its trust made for the 2026-05-31 period, and its first holdings filing is due 2026-08-29 or 2026-09-29. Its registration statement says only that it "seeks to provide full exposure to each of the Managed Futures Strategy and the U.S. Equity Strategy, simultaneously" and that "aggregate notional exposure will exceed its net assets". THE STRUCTURE ABOVE IS RSST'S, COPIED. That is the least arbitrary assumption available: it makes the JPFP arm differ from the RSST arm by its 40 bp fee and by nothing else. It is an assumption, not a measurement.
funds.error: Everything except the 59 bp unitary fee is assumed, including the 0.331 futures share below, which is RSST's. "Not filed, with a date attached" is the honest state of this fund and no number here changes it. JPFP's entire measurable advantage in this tournament is 40 bp of fee against RSST, which at a 30% weight is 12 bp/yr on the portfolio by construction: two orders of magnitude below this design's resolution for a stacked arm. The arm exists to show that, not to rank the fund. It also expects to create and redeem in cash, which forfeits the in-kind tax shield on its equity leg as well as its overlay.

haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.

haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.
mapping_perturbation.reporting: Report the minimum and maximum gap over the 27-point grid for every arm, and mark an arm `unresolved` under falsifier clause (e) if its gap changes sign anywhere on the grid. A ranking that survives only at the central point is a property of the mapping.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: This table is arithmetic on the window length and a grid of tracking errors. It required no look at the data and it is the reason this specification predicts, in advance, that most arms will come back `unresolved`.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, where `sigma_gap` is the annualised standard deviation of the paired monthly difference in log returns between an arm and its benchmark. The multiplier is `z(0.975) + z(0.80)`.
minimum_detectable_effect.what_this_says: Two arms differing only in weighting method over the same seven sleeves will track each other within 1-3 percentage points, so this design can resolve differences of roughly 0.5 to 1.4 pp/yr between them. An arm holding 30% trend notional will track the cap-weighted control at 5-8 percentage points, so this design can resolve nothing below roughly 2.4 to 3.8 pp/yr for it. THE TOURNAMENT IS THEREFORE WELL POWERED FOR THE WEIGHTING-METHOD QUESTION AND BADLY POWERED FOR THE STACKED-WRAPPER QUESTION, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing it can report.

multiple_testing_family.family: Every contestant scored against `control_capweight` on the primary metric over the full joint window, excluding the benchmarks themselves. One family per benchmark; the families are never pooled.
multiple_testing_family.what_the_family_omits: It omits the sub-period tests, the perturbation grid, the haircut sweeps, the hostile arms, and every one of the fifteen earlier specifications that searched this same data. It also omits the candidate weights that were considered and discarded before this file was written, which are not recoverable. The corrected p-values are therefore an UPPER BOUND on significance, exactly as `TRIALS_CAVEAT` in `portfolio_edge.experiments.ledger` says a specification count is an upper bound on trials.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS before any statistic is computed. Ken French recomputes his files from each new CRSP vintage and AQR reconstructs its entire history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a NEW VINTAGE rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. A normalised-hash mismatch when the raw hash matched means the parser changed behaviour, which is a finding and not a hash to update.

weighting_method_estimation.covariance_input: monthly excess returns of the mapped sleeves
weighting_method_estimation.note: An in-sample optimisation would be a look-ahead and is not run. The in-sample result is reported for the minimum-variance arm ONLY, labelled `lookahead_ceiling`, so that the reader can see the size of the gap between what an optimiser would have achieved knowing the answer and what it achieved not knowing it. That figure is a diagnostic and scores nothing.
weighting_method_estimation.scored_window: 1990-11 plus 120 months is 2000-11, so every weighting-method arm is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, 307 months. ITS BENCHMARK IS RE-MEASURED ON THE SAME 307 MONTHS. A weighting-method gap and a constant-weight gap are computed on different windows and are never placed in the same ranking column, and the two Benjamini-Hochberg families are separate for the same reason.
weighting_method_estimation.window: expanding, ending the month before the rebalance

years_to_distinguish.definition: The holding period at which this design's own detection floor falls to the arm's estimated gap: `years = (2.801585 * sigma_gap / gap)**2`, the inversion of the minimum-detectable-effect formula. It answers the question an investor actually faces, which is not "which construction has the larger expected value" but "how long would I have to hold this before I could tell whether it worked".
years_to_distinguish.reporting: Reported beside every gap. WHERE IT EXCEEDS A HUMAN INVESTING HORIZON THAT IS A HEADLINE FINDING AND NOT A CAVEAT: it means the ranking is a ranking of expected values whose differences are unobservable to the person holding them, which reframes the decision from "which is best" to "which is best-supported and cheapest to be wrong about".

notes: numbers printed to the console by the --view-results flag of exp_016_construction_tournament

assumed_fee_grid.rationale: AVES's fee appears nowhere in this repository. The grid brackets the plausible range and the headline uses the middle point, labelled as an assumption everywhere it appears.

alt_idmo_swap_trend22.note: The construction that survived all three of that study's alpha-charging conventions: US large value out, developed ex-US momentum and cheap core in, trend cut from 30% to 22%. alt_idmo_swap_trend30.note: The same sleeve substitution with the trend weight LEFT at 30%, so that the substitution and the trend cut can be told apart. Neither arm alone can attribute a difference to one of them.

control_capweight_levered.note: 1.3216 is `proposal_rsst`'s gross notional: 0.30 x 2.072 + 0.70. control_global_603010.note: The `control` in `src/content/portfolios.ts`, whose 60/30/10 split that file calls a declared research weight rather than a market weight.

erc_engines.note: The charter says to count distinct return engines and failure modes rather than ticker symbols, and no experiment here has ever weighted by engine. erc_engines.role: candidate of this experiment's own design

fund_cash_30.note: The same portfolio as `fund_prorata_30`, scored against the cash-holding investor's own counterfactual.

fund_overlay_103.note: The low end of the variance-minimising trend notional's supported interval, `w* = -rho sigma_equity / sigma_trend` with rho in [-0.277, -0.088] at one standard error.

fund_overlay_30.note: 100% of the control plus 30% trend notional financed on top. Gross 1.30.

fund_overlay_328.note: The high end of the same interval. With 10.3, 21.6, 30.0 and 32.8 all run, a growth argument and a variance argument can be compared directly instead of asserted to agree.

fund_prorata_30.note: The control sold pro rata to fund the sleeve. Gross 1.00. THIS ARM AND `fund_cash_30` HOLD THE IDENTICAL PORTFOLIO; only the benchmark differs, which is the entire point of running both.

proposal_mate_prospectus_floor.note: MATE priced at its prospectus contractual floor of 100% equity (delta 0.00) rather than at the 115.87% its 2026-05-31 filing shows (delta -0.159), because the filed index future cannot be separated into base completion and the trend book's own equity position. proposal_no_trend.note: The proposal with the wrapper replaced by plain US beta at the same capital. Nobody in this repository has separated them.

proposal_rsst.note: The investor's proposal, and identically the `candidate` in `src/content/portfolios.ts`. 132% gross exposure.

proposal_rsst_216.note: The proposal with the wrapper cut to the weight that delivers 21.6% of trend notional, the freed capital going to plain US beta. US equity notional falls from 67.2% to 66.6%, which is the price of holding the trend weight rather than the equity weight fixed.

proposal_ten_bp_wrapper.note: The proposal with an 89 bp cheaper wrapper and nothing else changed. The difference from `proposal_rsst` is 0.30 x 0.89 = 26.7 bp/yr, and it is the only difference in this whole tournament that is knowable in advance rather than estimated.

repo_evidence_led.note: The `evidence-led` candidate in `src/content/portfolios.ts`, at the weights its tilts were priced at.

stacked_heavy_50.note: Nobody in this repository has proposed more than 30% of a stacked wrapper. If 30% is right, this arm should be worse; if the wrapper's near-zero delta is the mechanism the funding algebra says it is, this arm should be better and the proposal's 30% is a habit rather than a result. Gross 1.536.
stacked_heavy_50.role: candidate of this experiment's own design

wm_market_weight.note: The market-weight member of decision 0009 clause 4's six, over the cap-weight vehicles.

wm_min_variance_shrunk.note: Ledoit-Wolf linear shrinkage to the constant-correlation target, intensity estimated on the same expanding window.

It answers a different question from the rest of the file -- "would an optimiser have chosen these weights" -- and it is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, a different window, in a separate Benjamini-Hochberg family. Its gap is never placed in a column with a constant-weight gap.

evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written, frozen and hashed before the experiment module produced any statistic. The DATA, however, has been searched by fifteen earlier specifications, and the weights, the fund list and the loadings were chosen by people who had read those results. That is the look-ahead that matters here and no freezing step removes it.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every ticker in this experiment is a linear combination of public factor series and a fee. No fund's returns were used, because none is committed. The tournament therefore scores CONSTRUCTIONS. A construction result transfers to a fund only to the extent that the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost, which experiments 002, 009, 013, 014 and 015 measured for the tilt funds and which nobody has measured for MATE or JPFP.

financing_basis_band.basis: 0.62% is the point estimate Experiments 016 and 016b charge: ten equity-index futures rolls Dec-2022 to Mar-2025 against 3-month Term SOFR, recorded in `docs/research/structural-and-tax-edges.md` section 3 as of 2026-08-16. The 0.98% to 2.31% endpoints are the break-even financing band derived for a trend overlay elsewhere in this repository. The grid spans both.
financing_basis_band.reporting: Report whether the ordering of the watched wrapper arms is the same at every point of the band. IF IT IS NOT, THE RANKING OF THOSE ARMS IS NOT A FINDING and must not be presented as one. Note that the levered control carries more futures notional (0.3216) than any wrapper arm does, so a rising basis does not move every arm the same way; it charges the benchmark hardest.

fund_mapping.doctrine: ticker -> basis expression -> what the mapping assumes -> what error it introduces. Loadings are this repository's own measured values from `src/content/shelf.ts` as of 2026-08-17. A market beta of 1.000 is an assumption everywhere: no market beta was measured for any of these funds.

JPFP commenced operations on 2026-05-27 with $17.07m of net assets and has filed no Form N-PORT; its series S000101300 appears in none of the 24 filings its trust made for the 2026-05-31 period, and its first holdings filing is due 2026-08-29 or 2026-09-29. Its registration statement says only that it "seeks to provide full exposure to each of the Managed Futures Strategy and the U.S. Equity Strategy, simultaneously" and that "aggregate notional exposure will exceed its net assets". THE STRUCTURE ABOVE IS RSST'S, COPIED. That is the least arbitrary assumption available: it makes the JPFP arm differ from the RSST arm by its 40 bp fee and by nothing else. It is an assumption, not a measurement.

"Not filed, with a date attached" is the honest state of this fund and no number here changes it. JPFP's entire measurable advantage in this tournament is 40 bp of fee against RSST, which at a 30% weight is 12 bp/yr on the portfolio by construction: two orders of magnitude below this design's resolution for a stacked arm. The arm exists to show that, not to rank the fund. It also expects to create and redeem in cash, which forfeits the in-kind tax shield on its equity leg as well as its overlay.

haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.
mapping_perturbation.reporting: Report the minimum and maximum gap over the 27-point grid for every arm, and mark an arm `unresolved` under falsifier clause (e) if its gap changes sign anywhere on the grid. A ranking that survives only at the central point is a property of the mapping.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: This table is arithmetic on the window length and a grid of tracking errors. It required no look at the data and it is the reason this specification predicts, in advance, that most arms will come back `unresolved`.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, where `sigma_gap` is the annualised standard deviation of the paired monthly difference in log returns between an arm and its benchmark. The multiplier is `z(0.975) + z(0.80)`.
minimum_detectable_effect.what_this_says: Two arms differing only in weighting method over the same seven sleeves will track each other within 1-3 percentage points, so this design can resolve differences of roughly 0.5 to 1.4 pp/yr between them. An arm holding 30% trend notional will track the cap-weighted control at 5-8 percentage points, so this design can resolve nothing below roughly 2.4 to 3.8 pp/yr for it. THE TOURNAMENT IS THEREFORE WELL POWERED FOR THE WEIGHTING-METHOD QUESTION AND BADLY POWERED FOR THE STACKED-WRAPPER QUESTION, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing it can report.

multiple_testing_family.family: Every contestant scored against `control_capweight` on the primary metric over the full joint window, excluding the benchmarks themselves. One family per benchmark; the families are never pooled.
multiple_testing_family.what_the_family_omits: It omits the sub-period tests, the perturbation grid, the haircut sweeps, the hostile arms, and every one of the fifteen earlier specifications that searched this same data. It also omits the candidate weights that were considered and discarded before this file was written, which are not recoverable. The corrected p-values are therefore an UPPER BOUND on significance, exactly as `TRIALS_CAVEAT` in `portfolio_edge.experiments.ledger` says a specification count is an upper bound on trials.

premium_surface.basis: The equity grid is stated as a HAIRCUT and converted to an assumed premium against the panel's own realised US market excess return, which is reported in `panel_moments` rather than asserted here. 4.83 and 8.33 are the haircuts that land the assumed US equity premium on 5.00% and 1.50% respectively if the realised figure is 9.83%; the run recomputes the assumed premium from the panel and does not rely on that arithmetic. The trend grid is 016's haircut sweep extended by a point. Only the three regional MARKET legs are haircut. The value and momentum legs are left alone and swept separately, because this surface is about the equity-versus-trend substitution and a third dimension would make it unreadable rather than more honest.
premium_surface.reporting: Report the required GROSS trend premium at each assumed equity premium, and state plainly whether the sign of the overlay's contribution depends on the equity premium assumed. IF IT DOES, no conclusion about the overlay may be published against a single equity premium.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS before any statistic is computed. Ken French recomputes his files from each new CRSP vintage and AQR reconstructs its entire history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a NEW VINTAGE rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. A normalised-hash mismatch when the raw hash matched means the parser changed behaviour, which is a finding and not a hash to update.

weighting_method_estimation.covariance_input: monthly excess returns of the mapped sleeves
weighting_method_estimation.note: An in-sample optimisation would be a look-ahead and is not run. The in-sample result is reported for the minimum-variance arm ONLY, labelled `lookahead_ceiling`, so that the reader can see the size of the gap between what an optimiser would have achieved knowing the answer and what it achieved not knowing it. That figure is a diagnostic and scores nothing.
weighting_method_estimation.scored_window: 1990-11 plus 120 months is 2000-11, so every weighting-method arm is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, 307 months. ITS BENCHMARK IS RE-MEASURED ON THE SAME 307 MONTHS. A weighting-method gap and a constant-weight gap are computed on different windows and are never placed in the same ranking column, and the two Benjamini-Hochberg families are separate for the same reason.
weighting_method_estimation.window: expanding, ending the month before the rebalance

years_to_distinguish.definition: The holding period at which this design's own detection floor falls to the arm's estimated gap: `years = (2.801585 * sigma_gap / gap)**2`, the inversion of the minimum-detectable-effect formula. It answers the question an investor actually faces, which is not "which construction has the larger expected value" but "how long would I have to hold this before I could tell whether it worked".
years_to_distinguish.reporting: Reported beside every gap. WHERE IT EXCEEDS A HUMAN INVESTING HORIZON THAT IS A HEADLINE FINDING AND NOT A CAVEAT: it means the ranking is a ranking of expected values whose differences are unobservable to the person holding them, which reframes the decision from "which is best" to "which is best-supported and cheapest to be wrong about".

assumed_fee_grid.rationale: AVES's fee is NO LONGER AN ASSUMPTION: its quarterly fact sheet as of 2026-06-30, read on 2026-08-22 and recorded on the shelf, states 36 bp gross equal to net with no waiver and no expense cap. This file charges 36 where 016 charged an assumed 30, which is the one cost input that differs from 016b, and it is the reason a shared arm's growth may differ from 016's in the third decimal. The grid is retained as a pure sensitivity rather than as a statement that the fee is unknown. AVDV's 36 bp is read from its Form 497K dated 2025-12-31; the 50 bp point exists only to bound what an unread securities-lending credit or an unpriced trading cost could do to it.

avuv_for_vtv.note: `recommended` with AVUV substituted for VTV at the same 15% of capital. BOTH FUNDS ARE MAPPED ON THE SAME 72-MONTH WINDOW, 2020-01..2025-12, so the comparison is a legitimate one. On that window AVUV carries the deeper value exposure (+0.537 against +0.337) and 22 bp more fee. Gross 1.268.

avuv_for_vtv_matched_loadings.note: The AVUV variant with AVUV mapped at its matched-window HML of +0.467. THIS ARM AND THE ONE ABOVE ARE THE PAIR THAT MUST BE READ TOGETHER: on the matched window VTV's value exposure is HIGHER than AVUV's, reversing the published ordering, and the recommendation's VTV call must survive both readings or be reported as unresolved.
avuv_for_vtv_matched_loadings.role: sensitivity to the window a loading was fitted on

control_capweight_levered.note: The ORIGINAL eight-fund proposal's gross notional, 0.30 x 2.072 + 0.70. It keeps 016's name because the tournament module reads this arm's Sharpe ratio for falsifier clause (b). Financed at cash plus the declared equity-futures basis and charged on identical terms to the arms it benchmarks.

control_capweight_levered_1268.note: The RECOMMENDED construction's gross notional, 0.25 x 2.072 + 0.75, and identically the previous recommendation's and both AVUV variants' -- all four hold RSST at 25%. A second control exists because a 1.3216x benchmark is not leverage-matched to a 1.268x arm and 016's own scope note records that mismatch as a defect it could not avoid with a single control.

fund_cash_30.note: The same portfolio as `fund_prorata_30`, scored against the cash-holding investor's own counterfactual. The three funding arms are carried forward unchanged from 016b so that this file reproduces the funding wedge and so that a reader can locate its new arms against a known scale.

fund_overlay_30.note: 100% of the control plus 30% trend notional financed on top. Gross 1.30.

fund_prorata_30.note: The control sold pro rata to fund the sleeve. Gross 1.00. THIS ARM AND `fund_cash_30` HOLD THE IDENTICAL PORTFOLIO; only the benchmark differs.

investor_original_eight.note: Identically 016's `proposal_rsst` and the `candidate` in `src/content/portfolios.ts`. Gross 1.3216, so it is scored against the 1.3216x control and NOT against the 1.268x one. Its point estimate should reproduce 016's +2.49 pp/yr; a shared arm that moves is a defect in this file. Only its Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p may legitimately differ, because the family here is a different size.
investor_original_eight.role: the proposal the tournament originally scored

previous_no_trend.note: The same decomposition for the previous recommendation, so that the AVDV decision can be read on the unlevered tilt-only pair as well as on the levered whole-portfolio pair.

previous_recommendation.note: The recommendation before the tilt audit. It differs from `recommended` by nine points of VXUS and one of VTI moving into AVDV, and by nothing else, so the pair prices the AVDV decision inside a whole portfolio rather than as a standalone sleeve edge. Gross notional 1.268.

recommended.note: THE ARM THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. The portfolio this repository currently recommends, tested for the first time as a single object. Gross notional 1.268. Seven lines; three of them (VTI, VXUS) carry no active position at all against the control.

recommended_matched_loadings.note: `recommended` with VTV mapped at its MATCHED-WINDOW loading of +0.520 (36 months, 2023-01..2025-12) instead of its published +0.337 (72 months).
recommended_matched_loadings.role: sensitivity to the window a loading was fitted on

recommended_no_trend.note: The recommended construction with the wrapper replaced by plain US beta at the same capital. The difference from `recommended` is what the trend leg contributes; the difference from the cheap control is what the TILTS contribute. 016's equivalent arm returned +0.79 pp/yr against a 0.47 floor and was one of only three resolvable arms in that whole tournament.

recommended_vs_avuv.note: VTV against AVUV at 15% of capital, as a paired portfolio difference, on the published 72-month loadings. Same gross notional on both sides.

recommended_vs_original.note: The recommended construction scored DIRECTLY against the investor's original proposal rather than against a control. This is the comparison the recommendation actually claims to have won, and it has never been run. The two arms carry different gross notionals (1.268 against 1.3216), so five points of the difference is a leverage difference and the pair is not leverage-matched to each other. That is inherent in the comparison -- the recommendation cut the wrapper from 30% to 25% -- and it is stated rather than corrected away.

recommended_vs_previous.note: The AVDV decision, priced as a paired difference between two portfolios at the SAME gross notional differing in one sleeve. This is the tightest comparison in the file and therefore the one with the smallest detection floor.

wm_min_variance.note: Long-only minimum variance over the RECOMMENDED construction's own six unlevered sleeves, estimated walk-forward on an expanding window with a 120-month minimum and applied twelve months forward. It answers a different question from the rest of the file -- "would an optimiser have chosen these weights" -- and it is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, a different window, in a separate Benjamini-Hochberg family. Its gap is never placed in a column with a constant-weight gap.

haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.
mapping_perturbation.reporting: Report the minimum and maximum gap over the 27-point grid for every arm, and mark an arm `unresolved` under falsifier clause (e) if its gap changes sign anywhere on the grid. A ranking that survives only at the central point is a property of the mapping.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: This table is arithmetic on the window length and a grid of tracking errors. It required no look at the data and it is the reason this specification predicts, in advance, that most arms will come back `unresolved`.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, where `sigma_gap` is the annualised standard deviation of the paired monthly difference in log returns between an arm and its benchmark. The multiplier is `z(0.975) + z(0.80)`.
minimum_detectable_effect.what_this_says: Two arms differing only in weighting method over the same seven sleeves will track each other within 1-3 percentage points, so this design can resolve differences of roughly 0.5 to 1.4 pp/yr between them. An arm holding 30% trend notional will track the cap-weighted control at 5-8 percentage points, so this design can resolve nothing below roughly 2.4 to 3.8 pp/yr for it. THE TOURNAMENT IS THEREFORE WELL POWERED FOR THE WEIGHTING-METHOD QUESTION AND BADLY POWERED FOR THE STACKED-WRAPPER QUESTION, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing it can report.

multiple_testing_family.family: Every contestant scored against `control_capweight` on the primary metric over the full joint window, excluding the benchmarks themselves. One family per benchmark; the families are never pooled.
multiple_testing_family.what_the_family_omits: It omits the sub-period tests, the perturbation grid, the haircut sweeps, the hostile arms, and every one of the fifteen earlier specifications that searched this same data. It also omits the candidate weights that were considered and discarded before this file was written, which are not recoverable. The corrected p-values are therefore an UPPER BOUND on significance, exactly as `TRIALS_CAVEAT` in `portfolio_edge.experiments.ledger` says a specification count is an upper bound on trials.

premium_surface.basis: The equity grid is stated as a HAIRCUT and converted to an assumed premium against the panel's own realised US market excess return, which is reported in `panel_moments` rather than asserted here. 4.83 and 8.33 are the haircuts that land the assumed US equity premium on 5.00% and 1.50% respectively if the realised figure is 9.83%; the run recomputes the assumed premium from the panel and does not rely on that arithmetic. The trend grid is 016's haircut sweep extended by a point. Only the three regional MARKET legs are haircut. The value and momentum legs are left alone and swept separately, because this surface is about the equity-versus-trend substitution and a third dimension would make it unreadable rather than more honest.
premium_surface.reporting: Report the required GROSS trend premium at each assumed equity premium, and state plainly whether the sign of the overlay's contribution depends on the equity premium assumed. IF IT DOES, no conclusion about the overlay may be published against a single equity premium.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS before any statistic is computed. Ken French recomputes his files from each new CRSP vintage and AQR reconstructs its entire history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a NEW VINTAGE rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. A normalised-hash mismatch when the raw hash matched means the parser changed behaviour, which is a finding and not a hash to update.

weighting_method_estimation.covariance_input: monthly excess returns of the mapped sleeves
weighting_method_estimation.note: An in-sample optimisation would be a look-ahead and is not run. The in-sample result is reported for the minimum-variance arm ONLY, labelled `lookahead_ceiling`, so that the reader can see the size of the gap between what an optimiser would have achieved knowing the answer and what it achieved not knowing it. That figure is a diagnostic and scores nothing.
weighting_method_estimation.scored_window: 1990-11 plus 120 months is 2000-11, so every weighting-method arm is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, 307 months. ITS BENCHMARK IS RE-MEASURED ON THE SAME 307 MONTHS. A weighting-method gap and a constant-weight gap are computed on different windows and are never placed in the same ranking column, and the two Benjamini-Hochberg families are separate for the same reason.
weighting_method_estimation.window: expanding, ending the month before the rebalance

years_to_distinguish.definition: The holding period at which this design's own detection floor falls to the arm's estimated gap: `years = (2.801585 * sigma_gap / gap)**2`, the inversion of the minimum-detectable-effect formula. It answers the question an investor actually faces, which is not "which construction has the larger expected value" but "how long would I have to hold this before I could tell whether it worked".
years_to_distinguish.reporting: Reported beside every gap. WHERE IT EXCEEDS A HUMAN INVESTING HORIZON THAT IS A HEADLINE FINDING AND NOT A CAVEAT: it means the ranking is a ranking of expected values whose differences are unobservable to the person holding them, which reframes the decision from "which is best" to "which is best-supported and cheapest to be wrong about".

evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written, frozen and hashed before the experiment module produced any statistic. The DATA, however, has been searched by fifteen earlier specifications, and the weights, the fund list and the loadings were chosen by people who had read those results. That is the look-ahead that matters here and no freezing step removes it.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every ticker in this experiment is a linear combination of public factor series and a fee. No fund's returns were used, because none is committed. The tournament therefore scores CONSTRUCTIONS. A construction result transfers to a fund only to the extent that the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost, which experiments 002, 009, 013, 014 and 015 measured for the tilt funds and which nobody has measured for MATE or JPFP.

financing_basis_band.basis: 0.62% is the point estimate Experiments 016 and 016b charge: ten equity-index futures rolls Dec-2022 to Mar-2025 against 3-month Term SOFR, recorded in `docs/research/structural-and-tax-edges.md` section 3 as of 2026-08-16. The 0.98% to 2.31% endpoints are the break-even financing band derived for a trend overlay elsewhere in this repository. The grid spans both.
financing_basis_band.reporting: Report whether the ordering of the watched wrapper arms is the same at every point of the band. IF IT IS NOT, THE RANKING OF THOSE ARMS IS NOT A FINDING and must not be presented as one. Note that the levered control carries more futures notional (0.3216) than any wrapper arm does, so a rising basis does not move every arm the same way; it charges the benchmark hardest. The six single-holding arms at RSST 30 carry identical futures notional and the band cannot reorder them; it is the wrapper-weight pair the band is watched for.

haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.
mapping_perturbation.reporting: Report the minimum and maximum gap over the 27-point grid for every arm, and mark an arm `unresolved` under falsifier clause (e) if its gap changes sign anywhere on the grid. A ranking that survives only at the central point is a property of the mapping.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: This table is arithmetic on the window length and a grid of tracking errors. It required no look at the data and it is the reason this specification predicts, in advance, that most arms will come back `unresolved`.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, where `sigma_gap` is the annualised standard deviation of the paired monthly difference in log returns between an arm and its benchmark. The multiplier is `z(0.975) + z(0.80)`.
minimum_detectable_effect.what_this_says: Two arms differing only in weighting method over the same seven sleeves will track each other within 1-3 percentage points, so this design can resolve differences of roughly 0.5 to 1.4 pp/yr between them. An arm holding 30% trend notional will track the cap-weighted control at 5-8 percentage points, so this design can resolve nothing below roughly 2.4 to 3.8 pp/yr for it. THE TOURNAMENT IS THEREFORE WELL POWERED FOR THE WEIGHTING-METHOD QUESTION AND BADLY POWERED FOR THE STACKED-WRAPPER QUESTION, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing it can report.

multiple_testing_family.family: Every contestant scored against `control_capweight` on the primary metric over the full joint window, excluding the benchmarks themselves. One family per benchmark; the families are never pooled.
multiple_testing_family.what_the_family_omits: It omits the sub-period tests, the perturbation grid, the haircut sweeps, the hostile arms, and every one of the fifteen earlier specifications that searched this same data. It also omits the candidate weights that were considered and discarded before this file was written, which are not recoverable. The corrected p-values are therefore an UPPER BOUND on significance, exactly as `TRIALS_CAVEAT` in `portfolio_edge.experiments.ledger` says a specification count is an upper bound on trials.

premium_surface.basis: The equity grid is stated as a HAIRCUT and converted to an assumed premium against the panel's own realised US market excess return, which is reported in `panel_moments` rather than asserted here. 4.83 and 8.33 are the haircuts that land the assumed US equity premium on 5.00% and 1.50% respectively if the realised figure is 9.83%; the run recomputes the assumed premium from the panel and does not rely on that arithmetic. The trend grid is 016's haircut sweep extended by a point. Only the three regional MARKET legs are haircut. The value and momentum legs are left alone and swept separately, because this surface is about the equity-versus-trend substitution and a third dimension would make it unreadable rather than more honest. `rec30_vs_rec25` is watched here because freeze note 6(a) says its answer is a function of both premia.
premium_surface.reporting: Report the required GROSS trend premium at each assumed equity premium, and state plainly whether the sign of the overlay's contribution depends on the equity premium assumed. IF IT DOES, no conclusion about the overlay may be published against a single equity premium, and the wrapper-weight pair's sign is to be reported as a function of the premia and not as a number.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS before any statistic is computed. Ken French recomputes his files from each new CRSP vintage and AQR reconstructs its entire history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a NEW VINTAGE rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. A normalised-hash mismatch when the raw hash matched means the parser changed behaviour, which is a finding and not a hash to update.

weighting_method_estimation.covariance_input: monthly excess returns of the mapped sleeves
weighting_method_estimation.note: An in-sample optimisation would be a look-ahead and is not run. The in-sample result is reported for the minimum-variance arm ONLY, labelled `lookahead_ceiling`, so that the reader can see the size of the gap between what an optimiser would have achieved knowing the answer and what it achieved not knowing it. That figure is a diagnostic and scores nothing.
weighting_method_estimation.scored_window: 1990-11 plus 120 months is 2000-11, so every weighting-method arm is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, 307 months. ITS BENCHMARK IS RE-MEASURED ON THE SAME 307 MONTHS. A weighting-method gap and a constant-weight gap are computed on different windows and are never placed in the same ranking column, and the two Benjamini-Hochberg families are separate for the same reason.
weighting_method_estimation.window: expanding, ending the month before the rebalance

years_to_distinguish.definition: The holding period at which this design's own detection floor falls to the arm's estimated gap: `years = (2.801585 * sigma_gap / gap)**2`, the inversion of the minimum-detectable-effect formula. It answers the question an investor actually faces, which is not "which construction has the larger expected value" but "how long would I have to hold this before I could tell whether it worked".
years_to_distinguish.reporting: Reported beside every gap. WHERE IT EXCEEDS A HUMAN INVESTING HORIZON THAT IS A HEADLINE FINDING AND NOT A CAVEAT: it means the ranking is a ranking of expected values whose differences are unobservable to the person holding them, which reframes the decision from "which is best" to "which is best-supported and cheapest to be wrong about".

evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written, frozen and hashed before the experiment module produced any statistic. The DATA, however, has been searched by fifteen earlier specifications, and the weights, the fund list and the loadings were chosen by people who had read those results. That is the look-ahead that matters here and no freezing step removes it.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every ticker in this experiment is a linear combination of public factor series and a fee. No fund's returns were used, because none is committed. The tournament therefore scores CONSTRUCTIONS. A construction result transfers to a fund only to the extent that the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost, which experiments 002, 009, 013, 014 and 015 measured for the tilt funds and which nobody has measured for MATE or JPFP.

financing_basis_band.basis: 0.62% is the point estimate Experiments 016 and 016b charge: ten equity-index futures rolls Dec-2022 to Mar-2025 against 3-month Term SOFR, recorded in `docs/research/structural-and-tax-edges.md` section 3 as of 2026-08-16. The 0.98% to 2.31% endpoints are the break-even financing band derived for a trend overlay elsewhere in this repository. The grid spans both.
financing_basis_band.reporting: Report whether the ordering of the watched wrapper arms is the same at every point of the band. IF IT IS NOT, THE RANKING OF THOSE ARMS IS NOT A FINDING and must not be presented as one. Note that the levered control carries more futures notional (0.3216) than any wrapper arm does, so a rising basis does not move every arm the same way; it charges the benchmark hardest. The six single-holding arms at RSST 30 carry identical futures notional and the band cannot reorder them; it is the wrapper-weight pair the band is watched for.

JPFP commenced operations on 2026-05-27 with $17.07m of net assets and has filed no Form N-PORT; its series S000101300 appears in none of the 24 filings its trust made for the 2026-05-31 period, and its first holdings filing is due 2026-08-29 or 2026-09-29. Its registration statement says only that it "seeks to provide full exposure to each of the Managed Futures Strategy and the U.S. Equity Strategy, simultaneously" and that "aggregate notional exposure will exceed its net assets". THE STRUCTURE ABOVE IS RSST'S, COPIED. That is the least arbitrary assumption available: it makes the JPFP arm differ from the RSST arm by its 40 bp fee and by nothing else. It is an assumption, not a measurement.
funds.error: Everything except the 59 bp unitary fee is assumed, including the 0.331 futures share below, which is RSST's. "Not filed, with a date attached" is the honest state of this fund and no number here changes it. JPFP's entire measurable advantage in this tournament is 40 bp of fee against RSST, which at a 30% weight is 12 bp/yr on the portfolio by construction: two orders of magnitude below this design's resolution for a stacked arm. The arm exists to show that, not to rank the fund. It also expects to create and redeem in cash, which forfeits the in-kind tax shield on its equity leg as well as its overlay.

funds.assumes: The shelf's PUBLISHED loading, fitted on 72 months, 2020-01..2025-12, describes 1990-2026. VTV is a 3 bp cap-weighted large-value index fund and not a systematic tilt; it is in the recommended construction because it is the cheapest way to buy US value exposure, not because a measured return argues for it. Its own measured alpha is -2.60 pp/yr against a 3.28 pp/yr floor.
funds.error: VTV'S LOADING IS THE LEAST STABLE NUMBER ON THE US VALUE SHELF. Rolling 36-month windows over its 81 filed months give 46 estimates from +0.143 to +0.520 -- a range wider than the entire spread between the nine US value products on their matched window. +0.337 is one window's answer. `VTV_M` below carries the matched-window answer instead, and the pair is the sensitivity. The +/-0.15 perturbation grid spans +0.187 to +0.487 and therefore does NOT reach +0.520, which is why the second ticker exists rather than being left to the grid.

funds.assumes: The MATCHED-WINDOW refit: 36 months, 2023-01..2025-12, the longest window all nine US value products share, from `docs/research/loading-comparability-and-wrapper-exposure.md` section 4. Used only in `recommended_matched_loadings`, and only ever against `AVUV_M`, which is refitted on the same 36 months.
funds.error: Thirty-six months is roughly one market regime, and it is the most recent one, which is also the period the value spread was widest. This is not a better estimate than +0.337; it is a DIFFERENT window's estimate, and the two arms exist so that the VTV-versus-AVUV question is answered on both or on neither. No alpha was fitted on this window, so `VTV_M` is charged none in the alpha-charging hostile arm and its cell reads `not measured`.

funds.error: The +0.880 SMB leg is the largest of any US value product on the shelf and the size premium is +0.33 pp/yr against a 2.47 pp/yr detection floor: it is variance with no signable expectation. 87% of what AVUV delivers beyond VTV is size. funds.assumes: The matched-window HML refit, 36 months, 2023-01..2025-12, from the same table as `VTV_M`. haircut_sweep.rationale: A constant subtracted from every monthly observation of the leg inside the simulation, so volatility and every correlation are unchanged and the gap falls linearly. The trend grid exists because AQR's series is gross of the vendor's own trading costs by omission; the value grid exists because the US value premium on its own panel is +1.57 pp/yr against a 5.03 pp/yr detection floor and is not signable. The break-even is reported by linear interpolation between the bracketing grid points, which is exact for this construction.

mapping_perturbation.loading_rule: The delta is added to the MAGNITUDE of every non-market, non-trend coefficient, preserving its sign: `c -> c + delta * sign(c)`. A +0.662 HML becomes 0.812 or 0.512; a -0.394 CMA becomes -0.544 or -0.244. Market betas are not perturbed by this parameter and the trend beta has its own.
mapping_perturbation.reporting: Report the minimum and maximum gap over the 27-point grid for every arm, and mark an arm `unresolved` under falsifier clause (e) if its gap changes sign anywhere on the grid. A ranking that survives only at the central point is a property of the mapping.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: This table is arithmetic on the window length and a grid of tracking errors. It required no look at the data and it is the reason this specification predicts, in advance, that most arms will come back `unresolved`.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, where `sigma_gap` is the annualised standard deviation of the paired monthly difference in log returns between an arm and its benchmark. The multiplier is `z(0.975) + z(0.80)`.
minimum_detectable_effect.what_this_says: Two arms differing only in weighting method over the same seven sleeves will track each other within 1-3 percentage points, so this design can resolve differences of roughly 0.5 to 1.4 pp/yr between them. An arm holding 30% trend notional will track the cap-weighted control at 5-8 percentage points, so this design can resolve nothing below roughly 2.4 to 3.8 pp/yr for it. THE TOURNAMENT IS THEREFORE WELL POWERED FOR THE WEIGHTING-METHOD QUESTION AND BADLY POWERED FOR THE STACKED-WRAPPER QUESTION, and that asymmetry is the most useful thing it can report.

multiple_testing_family.family: Every contestant scored against `control_capweight` on the primary metric over the full joint window, excluding the benchmarks themselves. One family per benchmark; the families are never pooled.
multiple_testing_family.what_the_family_omits: It omits the sub-period tests, the perturbation grid, the haircut sweeps, the hostile arms, and every one of the fifteen earlier specifications that searched this same data. It also omits the candidate weights that were considered and discarded before this file was written, which are not recoverable. The corrected p-values are therefore an UPPER BOUND on significance, exactly as `TRIALS_CAVEAT` in `portfolio_edge.experiments.ledger` says a specification count is an upper bound on trials.

premium_surface.basis: The equity grid is stated as a HAIRCUT and converted to an assumed premium against the panel's own realised US market excess return, which is reported in `panel_moments` rather than asserted here. 4.83 and 8.33 are the haircuts that land the assumed US equity premium on 5.00% and 1.50% respectively if the realised figure is 9.83%; the run recomputes the assumed premium from the panel and does not rely on that arithmetic. The trend grid is 016's haircut sweep extended by a point. Only the three regional MARKET legs are haircut. The value and momentum legs are left alone and swept separately, because this surface is about the equity-versus-trend substitution and a third dimension would make it unreadable rather than more honest. `rec30_vs_rec25` is watched here because freeze note 6(a) says its answer is a function of both premia.
premium_surface.reporting: Report the required GROSS trend premium at each assumed equity premium, and state plainly whether the sign of the overlay's contribution depends on the equity premium assumed. IF IT DOES, no conclusion about the overlay may be published against a single equity premium, and the wrapper-weight pair's sign is to be reported as a function of the premia and not as a number.

source_pin.pin_policy: A raw-hash mismatch ABORTS before any statistic is computed. Ken French recomputes his files from each new CRSP vintage and AQR reconstructs its entire history on every update, so an unrecognised hash is a NEW VINTAGE rather than a corrupted download, and a result computed from an unrecognised file looks exactly like a good one. A normalised-hash mismatch when the raw hash matched means the parser changed behaviour, which is a finding and not a hash to update.

weighting_method_estimation.covariance_input: monthly excess returns of the mapped sleeves
weighting_method_estimation.note: An in-sample optimisation would be a look-ahead and is not run. The in-sample result is reported for the minimum-variance arm ONLY, labelled `lookahead_ceiling`, so that the reader can see the size of the gap between what an optimiser would have achieved knowing the answer and what it achieved not knowing it. That figure is a diagnostic and scores nothing.
weighting_method_estimation.scored_window: 1990-11 plus 120 months is 2000-11, so every weighting-method arm is scored on 2000-11..2026-05, 307 months. ITS BENCHMARK IS RE-MEASURED ON THE SAME 307 MONTHS. A weighting-method gap and a constant-weight gap are computed on different windows and are never placed in the same ranking column, and the two Benjamini-Hochberg families are separate for the same reason.
weighting_method_estimation.window: expanding, ending the month before the rebalance

years_to_distinguish.definition: The holding period at which this design's own detection floor falls to the arm's estimated gap: `years = (2.801585 * sigma_gap / gap)**2`, the inversion of the minimum-detectable-effect formula. It answers the question an investor actually faces, which is not "which construction has the larger expected value" but "how long would I have to hold this before I could tell whether it worked".
years_to_distinguish.reporting: Reported beside every gap. WHERE IT EXCEEDS A HUMAN INVESTING HORIZON THAT IS A HEADLINE FINDING AND NOT A CAVEAT: it means the ranking is a ranking of expected values whose differences are unobservable to the person holding them, which reframes the decision from "which is best" to "which is best-supported and cheapest to be wrong about".

cond36_below0.note: PRIMARY. On when the trailing 36-month correlation through t-1 is below zero.

cond36_below_median120.note: On when the 36-month correlation is below the median of its own trailing 120 values; a relative rule with no fixed threshold.

cond36_below_minus02.note: The stricter threshold; on less often.

evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written and frozen, with its predictions, before the experiment module produced any statistic.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every wrapper is an assumed per-dollar exposure vector and a fee. The experiment scores constructions on public series; a result transfers to a fund only to the extent the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost. The arms were chosen by people who had read exp_018's artifact, including its era table; that look-ahead is recorded and no freezing removes it. The thresholds and windows were fixed by convention (36 and 60 months are the standard rolling-correlation windows; zero and -0.2 are the thresholds the mechanism names) before any conditioned path was simulated.

financing_sensitivity.reporting: Report every scored gap at every point and whether its sign survives; clause (d) reads the sign.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: Arithmetic on window length and a grid of tracking errors. Full window from 1929-07, 1151 months (95.9 years): 0.286 pp/yr per point of tracking error. Complement of the bond bull market from 1929-07, about 685 months (57.1 years): 0.371 per point. The 60-month arm loses 24 further months and the median arm 120 further months at the start.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, sigma_gap the annualised sd of the paired monthly difference.
minimum_detectable_effect.expected_gap: The certain cost of the leg is 11.4 bp/yr while on (0.2 x (39 + 15 + 0.10 x 62) - 0.2 x 3). With the on-state bond excess return unknown, 4 pp/yr on 40% of months gives 0.2 x 4 x 0.4 - 0.114 x 0.4 - switching, about +0.25 pp/yr: BELOW EVERY FLOOR ABOVE. On the complement the on-fraction is expected to be lower and the on-state bond excess return lower still.

expected_tracking_error_against_referenc.note: about 1.71 sqrt(f) points, f the fraction of months on; exp_018 measured 1.71 for the always-on stack

predicted_descriptives.complement_gap_vs_reference: between -0.2 and +0.2 pp/yr, inside its floor
predicted_descriptives.episode_1977_81_offset_vs_reference: between -8 and +2 pp; the unconditional stack read -22
predicted_descriptives.episode_2022_offset_vs_reference: about -2.4 pp, the same as the unconditional stack, because the rule is on

correlation_states.persists: The post-2020 positive correlation persists: the conditioned rule is off in every month (gap zero, no switches), the unconditional stack is on with rho = the after_bond_bull realised correlation.
correlation_states.reverts: The correlation reverts to its history: the conditioned rule is on the fraction of months it was on over the full window with rho = the on-state forward realised correlation, and pays its realised switching cost per year; the unconditional stack is on always with rho = the full-window realised correlation.

regret.formula: Expected annual log-growth gap of holding a w-point financed leg = f x [w x tp - certain_cost - (w^2 sigma_b^2 + 2 w rho sigma_p sigma_b)/2] - switching_cost_per_year, with f the on-fraction, tp the term premium, sigma_b and sigma_p the realised bond and reference volatilities, and rho the state's correlation. Regret of adopting = max(0, -gap); regret of not adopting = max(0, gap). The minimax action across the grid is reported for the conditioned stack, the unconditional stack and holding neither. Arithmetic on stated inputs; no interval, no status.

minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, sigma_gap the annualised sd of the paired monthly difference.
minimum_detectable_effect.expected_tracking_errors: Carry stack 10 against reference: about 0.10 x 12.38 = 1.2 points, floor 0.35 (primary), 0.48 (sub-window), 0.54 (secondary), 0.98 (check). Carry stack 20: 2.5 points, floor 0.71 / 0.97 / 1.08 / 1.96. Trend 15 / carry 15 against reference: about 0.15 x 12.38 x sqrt(2) = 2.6 points at zero correlation, floor 0.75 / 1.03 / 1.15. Carry 30 alone against cheap, and trend 30 + carry 30 against reference: about 3.7 points, floor 1.06 / 1.45 / 1.62. A 10-point stack of a leg earning 6 to 10 pp/yr gross per unit of notional contributes 0.6 to 1.0 pp/yr before an 11 bp certain cost: ABOVE the primary floor at the gross series and full loading, and at or below it under a 2 pp/yr haircut and a 0.681 loading.

panels.note: The longest window on which equity, T-bills, the own trend book and the carry composite all exist. Expected 1929-01..2025-05, 1157 months; the composite holds three asset classes before 1974-02.
The primary panel from the first month the currency carry leg exists. Expected 616 months.
AQR TSMOM replaces the own book; 1985-01..2026-02, the carry file's end. Expected 494 months.
A CHECK, NOT A TEST: 150 months after the carry paper circulated, on which no floor under about 1 pp/yr exists for any carry arm.
The primary panel with 1.0 pp/yr charged on every unit of carry notional.
The primary panel with 2.0 pp/yr charged on every unit of carry notional, the pessimistic bound.
The primary panel with the carry leg delivered at 0.681 of a unit, the loading RSST's filings show for its trend leg, applied here to the sister wrapper as an assumption; the fee is unchanged.

The primary panel with the carry series moved one month later. bridge.definition: OLS slope of the French factor on the VME leg over 1990-11..2026-05, both in decimal monthly returns, no intercept constraint. loading_perturbation.rule: Added to the magnitude of every non-market French coefficient before mapping, preserving sign, as in 016e. Reported as a range; clause (d).

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_the_run: Primary window 112 months, 9.333 years. Floor at 80% power is `2.801585 * TE / sqrt(9.333)`: 0.46 at 0.5% tracking error, 0.92 at 1.0%, 1.38 at 1.5%, 1.83 at 2.0%. The unscaled VME exposures imply a tracking error of roughly 1.0 to 1.2% from the legs' own volatilities, so the floor is about 0.9 to 1.1 pp/yr. Against a true effect of +0.8 that is roughly 60% power. THE PRIMARY TEST IS UNDERPOWERED FOR A FULL-SIZE REPLICATION AND WELL POWERED FOR A LARGE NEGATIVE, and that asymmetry is declared here.

minimum_detectable_effect.predicted_primary_pair: About -0.6 pp/yr arithmetic on the primary panel against a floor of about 0.35, interval excluding zero: `rejected` under clause (a). About -0.9 on the tournament panel against a floor of about 0.6: `rejected`. Freeze note 5.

regret.gold_grid_source: The repository holds no forward gold premium estimate; the alternative-sleeves audit reads gold as cash with swings, and 5.2 is the 1968-2025 realised figure backed out of 018. 0.0 is the central by declaration and is the conservative reading.

regret.what: Each candidate's expected gap against `cautious` at forward premia, arithmetic on the capital-weight difference and no simulation. A1: `X x (t - 0.97 - f_T + 0.05)`, t the gross trend premium per unit of notional at 12.38% volatility, f_T the Treasury financing in pp. A2: `X x (lambda t - 0.85 + 0.05 - b)`, lambda the delivered trend loading (1.0 and 0.671), b the ten-year's excess over cash. A3: `X x (0.9 g - 0.20 - 0.9 f_G + 0.9 x 0.03 + 0.1 x 0.05 - 0.1 b)`, g the gold excess over cash, f_G the gold financing. The log cell adds one constant per arm, half the difference of the arm's and the reference's realised variances on the arm's scored primary panel. A positive cell means the candidate wins. The break-even engine premium is printed beside each table. Freeze note 6 (a4) reads the cell at the central premia.

gde10.note: Tilt book scaled to 0.26 plus 0.09 of wrapper equity plus 0.1608 = 0.5108 equity; 0.150 trend; 0.490 bond; 0.090 gold.

reproduction.note: 016f run `36f14b39...`, reproduced by 024 and 025; a shared pair that moves is a defect in this file.

tournament_panel.weights_note: Tournament weights are rounded to three places and must sum to one; rounding moves equity notional by under 0.004 and the artifact prints each arm's exact notional.
tournament_panel.what: 016f's panel, basis mapping and cost model, loaded from its frozen file and checked against the hash its run `36f14b39...` recorded, with the ten-year leg added as 024 and 025 added it (`TSY10` mapped 1.000 to the Shiller/FRED GS10 par bond less French `RF` at 5 bp), the LBMA gold leg added as `gold` (spot excess of the panel's cash), and three wrappers mapped: `RSBT_LIKE` = 1.000 treasury + 1.000 trend at 112 bp, `TREND_FUND` = 1.000 trend at 85 bp, `GDE_LIKE` = 0.900 us_mkt + 0.900 gold at 47 bp. Annual rebalancing, 016f's clock. The tilt book is 016f's `rec30` equity lines (VTI 19 / VTV 15 / VXUS 16 / AVDV 10 / IDMO 5 / AVES 5) scaled whole to each arm's unlevered equity capital, so the tilt complex keeps its proportions; the GDE-like arms therefore shift the equity mix toward US large-cap as gold grows, which is what the fund does.

trend_book.scaling: One constant, `12.38 / realised full-window volatility of the book on the primary intersection of book, equity, cash and ltr`, 018's construction; printed in the artifact and checked against 018's figure to three places.

GDE_LIKE.note: Assumed: 90% physical equity plus 90% gold futures, financed at the gold rate, at 20 bp; 018's wrapper unchanged. Gold panels only.

RSBT_LIKE.note: Assumed: 100% Treasury futures over T-bill collateral plus a 100% trend book, at 97 bp. The bond leg is THE SAME modelled ten-year as the cautious portfolio's bond line, financed at the Treasury rate, so the pair against `cautious` differs by the trend leg and its costs alone. 018's RSBT_LIKE carried the ~20-year `ltr` leg; freeze note 3.

RSST_LIKE.note: RSST's N-PORT of 2026-04-30 as exp_016, 018, 024 and 025 map it. Financing on the 0.331 of equity futures at the equity rate.

TREND_FUND.note: Assumed: an unlevered managed-futures fund delivering 1.0 of the trend book at 85 bp (DBMF's fee). The 0.671 delivered loading measured in trend-marginal-value enters the regret table, not the path.

TSY10.note: An unlevered modelled ten-year Treasury at 5 bp; the TIPS line's proxy, freeze note 4.

crisis_episodes.note: 018's eight episodes, frozen there and copied unchanged, plus calendar 2022 so the rate shock can be read both to the trough and to the year end. Freeze note 6 (a3) reads `decision_episodes` on the primary panel.

drawdown_reporting.rule: For each panel and era, print every arm's worst fall and months under water in one table beside `cautious`'s, and the difference arm minus reference. Freeze note 6 (a2) reads the full window, from_1934 and the tournament full window; it carries no status.

evaluation_disclosure.order_of_operations: This file was written and frozen before any experiment module for it existed and before any statistic was produced. The arms were chosen by people who had read 018, 024, 025 and the candidates note of 2026-09-04; that look-ahead is recorded and no freezing removes it.
evaluation_disclosure.statement: Every holding is an assumed per-dollar exposure vector and a fee, or 016f's basis expression. No fund's returns were used. The experiment scores CONSTRUCTIONS; a result transfers to a fund only to the extent the fund delivers the mapped exposure at the mapped cost.

financing_sensitivity.reporting: Every arm's gap against `cautious` and against the cheap control at every point of every band that touches one of its legs, and whether the sign against `cautious` survives; clause (d) reads the union of the bands.

gold_leg.caveat: Spot excess of cash; the gold sub-window includes 1971-08..1974-12 when the dollar price was an administered peg being abandoned. Gold's real price stood at the 98.5th percentile of its 1975- record in September 2026 (alternative-sleeves audit); the regret table carries a 0.0 central.

minimum_detectable_effect.computed_before_freezing: Primary 1157 months: 0.285 pp/yr per point of tracking error. Gold sub-window 685 months: 0.371. Tournament 427 months: 0.470. An RSBT-like pair adds X of a 12.4%-volatility leg: tracking error about 12.4 X, floors about 0.35 / 0.71 / 1.06 (primary), 0.7 / 1.4 / 2.1 (tournament at TSMOM's higher volatility). A trend-fund pair swaps X of a 7% ten-year for X of the trend book, nearly uncorrelated: about 14.5 X, floors 0.41 / 0.83 / 1.24. A GDE-like pair adds 0.9 X of an 18-19% leg: about 16.5 X, floors 0.61 / 1.22 / 1.84 on 685 months.
minimum_detectable_effect.definition: `2.801585 * sigma_gap / sqrt(years)`, sigma_gap the annualised sd of the paired monthly difference.
minimum_detectable_effect.predicted_primary_pairs: Freeze note 5: A1 +0.62 / +1.23 / +1.85 `exploratory`; A2 +0.48 / +0.96 / +1.44 marginal; A3 +0.39 / +0.79 / +1.18 `unresolved`; all inside the floor at forward premia.
